P0100.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Malfunction
P0100.description: The ECU detects a general electrical malfunction in the mass air flow (MAF) sensor circuit.

P0101.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Range/Performance
P0101.description: The mass air flow (MAF) sensor signal is outside the expected range or does not track engine load plausibly.

P0102.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Low Input
P0102.description: The MAF sensor reports an air flow value below the plausible minimum for current engine speed and load.

P0103.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit High Input
P0103.description: The MAF sensor reports an air flow value above the plausible maximum for current engine speed and load.

P0104.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Intermittent
P0104.description: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts or noise on the mass air flow (MAF) sensor circuit.

P0105.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Barometric Pressure Circuit Malfunction
P0105.description: The ECU detects a general electrical malfunction in the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) or barometric pressure sensor circuit.

P0106.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0106.description: The manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor signal is implausible relative to throttle position and engine speed.

P0107.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Low Input
P0107.description: The MAP sensor reports a pressure below the lower threshold the ECU expects at any engine state.

P0108.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor High Input
P0108.description: The MAP sensor reports a pressure above the upper threshold the ECU expects in any engine state.

P0109.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Barometric Pressure Circuit Intermittent
P0109.description: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts on the MAP/BARO sensor circuit.

P010A.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit

P010E.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P010E.description: Intermittent signal from MAF sensor B.

P010F.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A/B Correlation
P010F.description: MAF sensor A and B disagree beyond plausible deviation.

P0110.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0110.description: The ECU detects a general electrical fault in the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor circuit.

P0111.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P0111.description: The intake air temperature (IAT) sensor reading does not change plausibly with engine warm-up or after driving begins.

P0112.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Low Input
P0112.description: The IAT signal voltage is below threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly hot intake (low NTC resistance).

P0113.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor High Input
P0113.description: The IAT signal voltage is above threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly cold intake (open-circuit-like behaviour).

P0114.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Intermittent
P0114.description: The IAT signal shows intermittent dropouts or jumps that fall outside slope expectations but do not stay above or below threshold long enough to trigger P0112/P0113.

P0115.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0115.description: A general fault has been detected in the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor circuit.

P0116.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P0116.description: The coolant temperature sensor reading does not change plausibly during warm-up, or its value disagrees with the intake air temperature when the engine has been off long enough that they should match.

P0117.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Low Input
P0117.description: The ECT signal voltage is below threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly hot coolant temperature (typical NTC sensor characteristic — low resistance at high temperature).

P0118.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor High Input
P0118.description: The ECT signal voltage is above threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly cold temperature (open-circuit-like behaviour).

P0119.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0119.description: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts on the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor circuit.

P011A.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P011A.description: ECT sensors 1 and 2 readings disagree beyond plausible limits — typically near startup both should match within tolerance.

P011B.title: Engine Coolant Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation
P011B.description: ECT and IAT readings disagree at long soak (engine off for hours) when both should match ambient.

P011C.title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 1
P011C.description: CAC temperature and IAT on bank 1 disagree at long soak.

P011D.title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 2
P011D.description: CAC temperature and IAT on bank 2 disagree at long soak.

P011E.title: Engine Coolant Temperature 1 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation
P011E.description: Engine Coolant Temperature 1 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation: the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern.

P011F.title: Engine Coolant Temperature 2 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation
P011F.description: Engine Coolant Temperature 2 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation: the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern.

P0120.title: Throttle Position Sensor / Switch A Circuit Malfunction
P0120.description: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the throttle position sensor/switch A circuit.

P0121.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Range/Performance
P0121.description: The throttle position sensor (TPS) signal does not match the expected range for the commanded pedal position.

P0122.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Low Input
P0122.description: The TPS signal voltage is below the lower acceptable threshold.

P0123.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" High Input
P0123.description: The TPS signal voltage exceeds the upper acceptable threshold.

P0124.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Circuit Intermittent
P0124.description: The TPS signal shows intermittent dropouts that do not stay outside threshold long enough to trigger P0122/P0123.

P0125.title: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Closed Loop Fuel Control
P0125.description: The engine has run long enough that closed-loop fuel control should be active, but the coolant temperature has not risen high enough.

P0126.title: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Stable Operation
P0126.description: Coolant temperature stays below the value expected for stable engine operation.

P0127.title: Intake Air Temperature Too High
P0127.description: Intake air temperature exceeds the safe maximum.

P0128.title: Coolant Thermostat Below Regulating Temperature
P0128.description: The engine has been running long enough to reach operating temperature, but coolant temperature stayed below the thermostat's regulating value.

P0129.title: Barometric Pressure Too Low
P0129.description: Barometric pressure reading below the plausible minimum.

P012A.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P012A.description: Generic electrical fault on turbo/supercharger inlet pressure sensor A.

P012B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P012B.description: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A reading implausible.

P012C.description: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A signal voltage below expected range.

P012D.description: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A signal voltage above expected range.

P012E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P012E.description: Intermittent signal from turbo inlet pressure sensor A.

P012F.title: Engine Coolant Temperature / Engine Oil Temperature Correlation
P012F.description: Engine coolant and oil temperature readings disagree beyond plausible limits.

P0130.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0130.description: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports an implausible signal — typically stuck mid-range, no switching between rich and lean, or no signal at all.

P0131.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0131.description: The upstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a low voltage, indicating the ECU sees a continuously lean exhaust on bank 1 — or the sensor signal path is shorted to ground.

P0132.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0132.description: The upstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a high voltage, indicating either a continuously rich exhaust on bank 1 or a short to supply voltage in the signal circuit.

P0133.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0133.description: The upstream oxygen sensor switches between rich and lean too slowly.

P0134.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0134.description: The ECU detects that the upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 shows no switching activity or responds too slowly to changing exhaust gas composition.

P0135.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0135.description: The heating element inside the upstream oxygen sensor draws no current, draws too much current, or is open-circuit.

P0136.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P0136.description: A general fault has been detected in the downstream (post-catalyst) oxygen sensor on bank 1.

P0137.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P0137.description: The downstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a low voltage.

P0138.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P0138.description: The downstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a high voltage, indicating either a continuously rich downstream reading (less common, since post-cat exhaust should be more stable) or a short to supply voltage in the signal circuit.

P0139.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0139.description: The ECU detects that the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports an abnormally high voltage signal, suggesting a persistently rich exhaust condition past the catalyst, a shorted sensor, or wiring shorted to a voltage source.

P013A.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2
P013A.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean.

P013B.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 2
P013B.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich.

P013C.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 2
P013C.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean.

P013D.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 2
P013D.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich.

P013E.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2
P013E.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean.

P013F.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 2
P013F.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich.

P0140.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0140.description: The ECU detects no switching or excessively slow response from the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1.

P0141.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P0141.description: The heating element inside the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 is open-circuit, drawing no current, or drawing too much.

P0142.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0142.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1.

P0143.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P0143.description: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the third oxygen sensor in the bank 1 exhaust path (typically located after a second catalyst on diesel or large engines with multi-cat exhausts).

P0144.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P0144.description: The ECU detects an abnormally low voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 1.

P0145.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P0145.description: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 1.

P0146.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P0146.description: The ECU detects no switching activity or too slow a response from the third O2 sensor on bank 1.

P0147.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P0147.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the third O2 sensor on bank 1.

P0148.title: Fuel Delivery Error
P0148.description: Fuel quantity actually delivered does not match the commanded value over a long observation window.

P014A.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 2
P014A.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean.

P014B.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 2
P014B.description: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich.

P014C.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 1
P014C.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean.

P014D.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 1
P014D.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich.

P014E.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 1

P014F.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 1
P014F.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich.

P0150.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P0150.description: Same condition as P0130 but on bank 2 of a multi-bank engine.

P0152.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P0152.description: Same condition as P0132 but on bank 2.

P0153.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0153.description: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the upstream O2 sensor on bank 2.

P0154.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0154.description: The ECU detects no switching activity or too slow a response from the upstream O2 sensor on bank 2.

P0155.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P0155.description: Same condition as P0135 but on the upstream sensor of bank 2.

P0157.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0157.description: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2.

P0158.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0158.description: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2 (alternate definition mapping in some manufacturers' interpretation).

P0159.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0159.description: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2.

P015A.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 1
P015A.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean.

P015B.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 1
P015B.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich.

P015C.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 1
P015C.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean.

P015D.description: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich.

P015E.title: Excessive Time to Enter Closed Loop Fuel Timing Control

P015F.title: Excessive Time to Enter Closed Loop Cylinder Balance Control
P015F.description: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop cylinder balance control.

P0160.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0160.description: The ECU detects no switching or too slow a response from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2.

P0161.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
P0161.description: Same condition as P0141 but on the downstream sensor of bank 2.

P0165.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 3)

P0166.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 3)

P0167.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P0167.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the third O2 sensor on bank 2.

P0168.title: Fuel Temperature Too High
P0168.description: Fuel temperature exceeds the safe maximum.

P016A.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control
P016A.description: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop air/fuel ratio control.

P016B.title: Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control At Limit - System Too Rich
P016B.description: Closed-loop fuel trim hit its lean correction limit because mixture is structurally too rich.

P016C.title: Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control At Limit - System Too Lean
P016C.description: Closed-loop fuel trim hit its rich correction limit because mixture is structurally too lean.

P016D.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control
P016D.description: ECU took longer than allowed to close the loop on fuel pressure control.

P016E.title: Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control At Limit - Pressure Too High
P016E.description: Closed-loop fuel pressure control hit its lower limit because rail pressure is structurally too high.

P016F.title: Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control At Limit - Pressure Too Low
P016F.description: Closed-loop fuel pressure control hit its upper limit because rail pressure is structurally too low.

P0170.title: Fuel Trim Malfunction (Bank 1)
