P043F.description: During the leak-detection self-test, airflow through the reference orifice is above the expected rate — typically a leak around the orifice or a damaged seal.

P0440.title: Evaporative Emission Control System Malfunction
P0440.description: A general fault in the evaporative emission (EVAP) system has been detected.

P0441.title: Evaporative Emission System Incorrect Purge Flow
P0441.description: The actual purge flow does not match the commanded value.

P0442.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
P0442.description: A small leak (typically equivalent to a 0.040 inch / 1.0 mm orifice) has been detected in the EVAP system.

P0443.title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit
P0443.description: Electrical fault in the EVAP purge solenoid circuit.

P0444.title: Evaporative Emission Purge Control Valve Circuit Open
P0444.description: The ECU has detected an open circuit in the purge solenoid control line — usually a broken wire, unplugged connector, or open coil winding.

P0445.title: Evaporative Emission System Purge Control Valve Circuit Shorted
P0445.description: The ECU detected a short in the EVAP purge solenoid control circuit.

P0446.title: Evaporative Emission Vent Control Circuit Malfunction
P0446.description: A fault in the EVAP vent valve circuit.

P0447.title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit Open
P0447.description: The ECU detected an open circuit on the EVAP vent valve control.

P0448.title: EVAP System Vent Control Circuit Shorted
P0448.description: EVAP vent valve drive circuit shorted to ground or B+.

P0449.title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Valve/Solenoid Circuit Malfunction
P0449.description: A general electrical fault was detected in the EVAP vent valve/solenoid control circuit.

P044A.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit
P044A.description: EGR Sensor C Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P044B.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P044B.description: EGR Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance: the signal is implausible or outside the valid range.

P044C.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit Low
P044C.description: EGR sensor C below lower plausibility — short to ground.

P044D.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit High
P044D.description: EGR sensor C above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+.

P044E.title: EGR Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P044E.description: EGR sensor C signal jumps or drops out intermittently.

P044F.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve A Circuit High
P044F.description: AIR switching valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+.

P0450.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
P0450.description: A general electrical fault on EVAP pressure sensor/switch A — used to monitor canister pressure during leak-detection diagnostics.

P0451.title: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0451.description: The fuel tank pressure sensor reading is implausible — for example, fluctuating signal, noise, or values that do not respond to known pressure events such as a key-on tank refill.

P0452.title: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor Low Input
P0452.description: The fuel tank pressure sensor signal is below the expected minimum voltage.

P0453.title: Evaporative Emission System Pressure Sensor High Input
P0453.description: The fuel tank pressure sensor signal is above the expected maximum voltage, typical of a short to supply or a sensor that has failed high.

P0454.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent
P0454.description: EVAP pressure sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently.

P0455.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
P0455.description: A large leak has been detected during the EVAP system pressure or vacuum test — large enough that the system cannot hold pressure for the diagnostic interval.

P0456.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
P0456.description: A very small leak (typically equivalent to a 0.020 inch / 0.5 mm orifice) has been detected.

P0457.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Fuel Cap Loose/Off)
P0457.description: The EVAP system detected a large leak that strongly correlates with a missing or improperly closed fuel filler cap.

P0458.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit Low
P0458.description: EVAP purge control valve A drive line stuck low — short to ground.

P0459.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Circuit High
P0459.description: EVAP purge control valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+.

P045A.title: EGR B Control Circuit
P045A.description: A general electrical fault on EGR control circuit B — second EGR valve on engines with high-pressure and low-pressure EGR loops.

P045B.title: EGR B Control Circuit Range/Performance
P045B.description: EGR valve B is electrically OK but does not respond as commanded — typically carbon buildup or sticking actuator.

P045C.title: EGR B Control Circuit Low
P045C.description: EGR B drive line stuck low — short to ground.

P045D.title: EGR B Control Circuit High
P045D.description: EGR B drive line stuck high — short to B+.

P045E.title: EGR B Control Stuck Open
P045E.description: EGR B Control Stuck Open: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P045F.title: EGR B Control Stuck Closed
P045F.description: EGR B Control Stuck Closed: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0460.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit
P0460.description: A general electrical fault on the primary fuel-level sensor (A) — open, shorted, or out of plausibility.

P0461.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0461.description: Fuel-level sensor A reads in range but plausibility check fails — value sticks, jumps, or does not match consumption.

P0462.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Low
P0462.description: Fuel-level sensor A below lower plausibility — short to ground.

P0463.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit High
P0463.description: Fuel-level sensor A above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+.

P0464.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0464.description: Fuel-level sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently.

P0465.title: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit
P0465.description: A general electrical fault on the EVAP purge flow sensor — measures actual flow through the purge valve to verify the canister is being purged.

P0466.title: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0466.description: EVAP purge flow sensor reads in range but plausibility check fails.

P0467.title: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit Low
P0467.description: EVAP purge flow sensor below lower plausibility — short to ground.

P0468.title: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit High
P0468.description: EVAP purge flow sensor above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+.

P0469.title: EVAP Purge Flow Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0469.description: EVAP purge flow sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently.

P046A.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 1)
P046A.description: Catalyst temperature sensors 1 and 2 on bank 1 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance over a drive cycle.

P046B.title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 2)
P046B.description: Catalyst temperature sensors 1 and 2 on bank 2 disagree by more than the allowed tolerance over a drive cycle.

P046C.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P046C.description: EGR sensor A reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.

P046D.title: EGR Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P046D.description: EGR sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently.

P046E.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P046E.description: EGR sensor B reads in range but plausibility check fails — slow response or stuck reading.

P046F.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P046F.description: EGR sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently.

P0470.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P0470.description: A general electrical fault on exhaust pressure sensor A — used to monitor backpressure across the DPF or to control variable-geometry turbo.

P0471.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0471.description: Exhaust pressure sensor A reads in range but plausibility check fails.

P0472.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P0472.description: Exhaust pressure sensor A below lower plausibility — short to ground.

P0473.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P0473.description: Exhaust pressure sensor A above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+.

P0474.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0474.description: Exhaust pressure sensor A signal jumps or drops out intermittently.

P0475.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A
P0475.description: A general fault on exhaust pressure control valve A — used as a backpressure brake on heavy-duty diesels and to assist DPF regeneration by raising exhaust temperature.

P0476.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Range/Performance
P0476.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A is electrically OK but does not move as commanded.

P0477.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Low
P0477.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A drive line stuck low — short to ground.

P0478.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A High
P0478.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A drive line stuck high — short to B+.

P0479.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Intermittent
P0479.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A drive signal is unstable.

P047A.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P047A.description: A general electrical fault on exhaust pressure sensor B — used to monitor backpressure across the DPF or to control variable-geometry turbo.

P047B.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P047B.description: Exhaust pressure sensor B reads in range but plausibility check fails.

P047C.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P047C.description: Exhaust pressure sensor B below lower plausibility — short to ground.

P047D.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P047D.description: Exhaust pressure sensor B above upper plausibility — open signal or short to B+.

P047E.title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P047E.description: Exhaust pressure sensor B signal jumps or drops out intermittently.

P047F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Open
P047F.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A is mechanically stuck open — backpressure cannot be raised, exhaust brake and DPF regen support fail.

P0480.title: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit
P0480.description: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.

P0481.title: Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit
P0481.description: Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.

P0482.title: Cooling Fan 3 Control Circuit Malfunction
P0482.description: Electrical fault detected in the third cooling fan control circuit.

P0483.title: Cooling Fan Rationality Check
P0483.description: The ECM detects that the cooling fan response does not match command.

P0484.title: Cooling Fan Current Too High
P0484.description: The current draw of the cooling fan exceeds the permitted maximum.

P0485.title: Cooling Fan Power/Ground Circuit
P0485.description: A fault is detected in the supply or ground path of the cooling fan circuit.

P0486.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit
P0486.description: A general electrical fault on EGR sensor B — second EGR sensor on dual-loop or HP/LP EGR systems.

P0487.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A/Open
P0487.description: The drive circuit of EGR throttle A is open.

P0488.title: EGR Throttle Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P0488.description: EGR throttle A is electrically OK but does not move as commanded.

P0489.title: EGR A Control Circuit Low
P0489.description: EGR A drive line stuck low — short to ground.

P048A.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Stuck Closed
P048A.description: Exhaust pressure control valve A is mechanically stuck closed — backpressure runs away, can stall the engine.

P048B.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit
P048B.description: A general electrical fault on the position sensor of exhaust pressure control valve A.

P048C.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P048C.description: Position sensor reads in range but plausibility check fails.

P048D.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P048D.description: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range.

P048E.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P048E.description: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range.

P048F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve A Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P048F.description: Position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently.

P0490.title: EGR A Control Circuit High
P0490.description: EGR A drive line stuck high — short to B+.

P0491.title: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 1)
P0491.description: AIR system flow on bank 1 is below threshold during the cold-start self-test — typically a clogged check valve, leaking hose, or weak air pump.

P0492.title: Secondary Air Injection System Insufficient Flow (Bank 2)
P0492.description: AIR system flow on bank 2 is below threshold during the cold-start self-test — typically a clogged check valve, leaking hose, or weak air pump.

P0493.title: Fan Overspeed
P0493.description: Fan Overspeed: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0494.title: Fan 1 Underspeed
P0494.description: Cooling fan 1 is rotating slower than commanded.

P0495.title: Fan 1 Overspeed
P0495.description: Fan 1 Overspeed: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0496.title: Evaporative Emission System High Purge Flow
P0496.description: The ECU detected EVAP purge flow during a non-purge condition, or higher than commanded purge flow.

P0497.title: EVAP System Low Purge Flow
P0497.description: The evaporative emissions system measures purge flow either via a dedicated purge flow sensor or via short-term fuel trim response when the purge valve opens.

P0498.title: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit Low
P0498.description: The vent valve closes the EVAP canister to atmosphere during leak tests.

P0499.title: EVAP System Vent Valve Control Circuit High
P0499.description: Same as P0498 with the control line open or shorted to supply.

P049A.title: EGR B Flow
P049A.description: The exhaust-gas recirculation system has a second EGR loop (B) - typically used on engines with a dedicated low-pressure EGR for emissions or on twin-bank V engines.

P049B.title: EGR B Flow Insufficient Detected
P049B.description: Same as P049A but specifically with measured flow below the required rate - typically EGR valve sticking closed or cooler heavily clogged.

P049C.title: EGR B Flow Excessive Detected
P049C.description: Same as P049A but with measured flow above the required rate - typically EGR valve sticking open or position sensor offset low.

P049D.title: EGR A Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P049D.description: EGR A Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P049E.title: EGR B Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P049E.description: EGR B Control Position Exceeded Learning Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P049F.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B
P049F.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the second exhaust pressure control valve (B) - used for example on dual exhaust brakes, twin-bank diesels with separate back-pressure flaps, or for DPF regeneration backpressure assist on the second bank.

P04A0.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Range or Performance
P04A0.description: Same as P049F with feedback in plausible range yet not matching the engine model - actuator slow, slipping or position sensor offset.

P04A1.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Low
P04A1.description: Same as P049F with the control line shorted to ground.

P04A2.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B High
P04A2.description: Same as P049F with the control line shorted to supply.

P04A3.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Intermittent
P04A3.description: Same as P049F with intermittent or erratic feedback - typically a connector or harness fault.

P04A4.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Stuck Open
P04A4.description: The exhaust pressure control valve B is mechanically stuck in the open position.

P04A5.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Stuck Closed
P04A5.description: Same as P04A4 but the valve B is stuck closed - back-pressure stays high even when the engine should run with low restriction; risk of overheating or excessive fuel consumption.

P04A6.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit
P04A6.description: A circuit fault is detected on the position sensor of exhaust pressure control valve B.

P04A7.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P04A7.description: Same as P04A6 with the signal in plausible range but not matching the actual valve angle.

P04A8.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit Low
P04A8.description: Same as P04A6 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P04A9.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit High
P04A9.description: Same as P04A6 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P04AA.title: Exhaust Pressure Control Valve B Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04AA.description: Same as P04A6 with intermittent or erratic feedback - typically a connector or harness fault.

P04AB.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit Open
P04AB.description: The second EVAP purge control valve (B) - used on systems with a divided purge path or on twin-bank engines - shows an open control circuit.

P04AC.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit Low
P04AC.description: Same as P04AB with the control line shorted to ground.

P04AD.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Circuit High
P04AD.description: Same as P04AB with the control line shorted to supply.

P04AE.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Performance Stuck Open
P04AE.description: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Performance Stuck Open: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P04AF.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve B Stuck Closed
P04AF.description: Same as P04AE but the valve B is stuck closed - no vapor purge possible through this stage, leading to elevated tank pressure and possible canister saturation.

P04B0.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit Open
P04B0.description: The refueling vapor control valve - typically part of the ORVR or capless fueling system - has an open control circuit.

P04B1.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit Low
P04B1.description: Same as P04B0 with the control line shorted to ground.

P04B2.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Circuit High
P04B2.description: Same as P04B0 with the control line shorted to supply.

P04B3.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Performance Stuck Open
P04B3.description: The refueling vapor control valve is stuck open.

P04B4.title: Refueling Vapor Control Valve Stuck Closed
P04B4.description: Same as P04B3 with the valve stuck closed - vapor cannot reach the canister during refueling, vapor escape from the filler is possible.

P04B5.title: Fuel Fill Door Stuck Open
P04B5.description: On vehicles with a motorised fuel fill door (no manual lever) the actuator and position switch report that the door is mechanically stuck open.

P04B6.title: Fuel Fill Door Stuck Closed
P04B6.description: Same as P04B5 with the door stuck closed - the user cannot refuel until the fault is cleared.

P04B7.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04B7.description: The position sensor or switch on the fuel fill door reports an intermittent signal - opens and closes randomly without matching the actual door position.

P04B8.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit
P04B8.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the fuel fill door position sensor or switch - the ECU cannot determine whether the door is open or closed.

P04B9.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit Low
P04B9.description: Same as P04B8 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P04BA.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit High
P04BA.description: Same as P04B8 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P04BB.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Circuit Open
P04BB.description: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Circuit Open: the control circuit is open.

P04BC.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Range or Performance
P04BC.description: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Range or Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P04BD.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Circuit Low
P04BD.description: Same as P04BB with the control line shorted to ground.

P04BE.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Control Circuit High
P04BE.description: Same as P04BB with the control line shorted to supply.

P04BF.title: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Circuit Open
P04BF.description: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Circuit Open: the control circuit is open.

P04C0.title: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Range or Performance
P04C0.description: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Range or Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P04C1.title: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Circuit Low
P04C1.description: Same as P04BD on the unlock side.

P04C2.title: Fuel Fill Door Unlock Control Circuit High
P04C2.description: Same as P04BE on the unlock side.

P04C3.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Position Sensor Circuit
P04C3.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the fuel fill door lock position sensor or switch.

P04C4.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Position Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P04C4.description: Same as P04C3 with feedback in plausible range yet not matching the commanded lock state.

P04C5.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Position Sensor Circuit Low
P04C5.description: Same as P04C3 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P04C6.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Position Sensor Circuit High
P04C6.description: Same as P04C3 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P04C7.title: Fuel Fill Door Lock Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04C7.description: Same as P04C3 with intermittent feedback.

P04C8.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit
P04C8.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the open-request input - the button or switch the driver presses to release the fuel fill door.

P04C9.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Performance Stuck Off
P04C9.description: The open-request switch never registers an active state - either the contact stays open mechanically or the wiring is permanently broken.

P04CA.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit Low
P04CA.description: Same as P04C8 with the signal voltage shorted to ground or constantly low.

P04CB.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit High
P04CB.description: Same as P04C8 with the signal voltage shorted to supply or constantly high.

P04CC.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04CC.description: Same as P04C8 with intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault.

P04CD.title: Fuel Fill Door Open Request Sensor or Switch Stuck On
P04CD.description: The open-request switch is stuck in the active state - the ECU continuously reads a request to open the fuel fill door.

P04CE.title: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit
P04CE.description: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P04CF.title: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit Range or Performance
P04CF.description: Same as P04CE with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model - typically sensor drift or a slow response after engine warm-up.

P04D0.title: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit Low
P04D0.description: Same as P04CE with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P04D1.title: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit High
P04D1.description: Same as P04CE with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P04D2.title: EGR Temperature Sensor C Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04D2.description: Same as P04CE with intermittent or erratic signal.

P04D3.title: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit
P04D3.description: The exhaust brake activation input - typically from a stalk lever, brake pedal switch, or vehicle bus message - shows a circuit fault.

P04D4.title: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit Range or Performance
P04D4.description: Same as P04D3 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching expected behaviour - e.g.

P04D5.title: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit Low
P04D5.description: Same as P04D3 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P04D6.title: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit High
P04D6.description: Same as P04D3 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P04D7.title: Exhaust Brake Input Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04D7.description: Same as P04D3 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P04D8.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop EGR Control
P04D8.description: After cold start the ECU operates EGR open-loop until preconditions (cooler temperature, sensor warm-up, engine load) are met, then transitions into closed-loop control.

P04D9.title: Closed Loop EGR Control At Limit Flow Too Low
P04D9.description: With EGR running in closed loop the controller has driven the actuator to its maximum opening but cannot reach the required EGR flow.

P04DA.title: Closed Loop EGR Control At Limit Flow Too High
P04DA.description: Same as P04D9 with the controller fully closing the actuator yet still measuring more EGR flow than required.

P04DB.title: Crankcase Ventilation System Disconnected
P04DB.description: A pressure or flow sensor in the crankcase ventilation (PCV) circuit reports atmospheric conditions where it should see crankcase or intake vacuum - the hose between crankcase and intake is disconnected, cracked, or open.

P04DC.title: Fuel Fill Door Position Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P04DC.description: Same as P04B8 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the actuator command - door reports closed when motor commanded open, or vice versa.

P04DD.title: Cold Start EGR A Flow Insufficient Detected
P04DD.description: During the cold-start strategy the ECU briefly opens EGR A to slow combustion temperatures and reduce engine-out NOx during catalyst light-off.

P04DE.title: Cold Start EGR A Flow Excessive Detected
P04DE.description: Same as P04DD with EGR flow above the cold-start target - typically valve sticking open during the cold phase or position sensor offset low.

P04DF.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Performance Stuck Open
P04DF.description: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Performance Stuck Open: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P04E0.title: EVAP System Purge Control Valve A Stuck Closed
P04E0.description: Same as P04AF on EVAP purge valve A.

P04E1.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit
P04E1.description: A dedicated sensor monitors whether the PCV hose is fitted to its connector at the engine.

P04E2.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Low
P04E2.description: Same as P04E1 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P04E3.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit High
P04E3.description: Same as P04E1 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P04E4.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04E4.description: Same as P04E1 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P04E5.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit
P04E5.description: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P04E6.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Range or Performance
P04E6.description: Same as P04CF on EGR temperature sensor D.

P04E7.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low
P04E7.description: Same as P04D0 on EGR temperature sensor D.

P04E8.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit High
P04E8.description: Same as P04D1 on EGR temperature sensor D.

P04E9.title: EGR Temperature Sensor D Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P04E9.description: Same as P04D2 on EGR temperature sensor D.

P04EA.title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side
P04EA.description: The EVAP leak diagnostic has detected a small leak on the fuel tank side of the system - typically a hose, gasket, fuel cap, or fuel sender flange that does not seal completely.

P04EB.title: EVAP System Small Leak Detected Fresh Air Side
P04EB.description: Same as P04EA but on the fresh-air side - the path between vent valve and atmosphere is not sealing completely during the active test phase.

P04EC.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side
P04EC.description: Same as P04EA but the leak is large enough that the system cannot build the test pressure or vacuum at all - typically a missing fuel cap, an unseated hose or a torn vapor line on the tank side.

P04ED.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected Fresh Air Side
P04ED.description: Same as P04EB on the fresh-air side, but with a leak large enough to prevent test build-up.

P04EE.title: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected Fuel Tank Side
P04EE.description: Same as P04EA but at the most sensitive leak threshold - typically the OBD-II 0.020-inch (~0.5 mm) test.

P04EF.title: EVAP System Very Small Leak Detected Fresh Air Side
P04EF.description: Same as P04EE on the fresh-air side - microcrack in a hose or imperfect vent valve seal at the most sensitive test threshold.

P04F0.title: EVAP System High Load Purge Line A Performance
P04F0.description: On engines that have a separate high-load purge line - to use boost pressure to pull vapor on turbo applications - the ECU monitors flow when this path is commanded.

P04F1.title: EVAP System Purge Line Performance
P04F1.description: A general performance fault on the EVAP purge line - flow does not match the requested rate, without specifying which segment.

P04F2.title: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 1
P04F2.description: The electric catalyst heater on bank 1 - used on hybrids and modern petrol cars to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature within seconds of cold start - reports that its supply voltage is outside the expected window.

P04F3.title: Catalyst Heater Supply Voltage Bank 2
P04F3.description: The electric catalyst heater on bank 2 - used on hybrids and modern petrol cars to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature within seconds of cold start - reports that its supply voltage is outside the expected window.

P04F4.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Low Bank 1
P04F4.description: The control or supply line to the electric catalyst heater on bank 1 is shorted to ground or measures below the expected voltage when the heater is commanded on.

P04F5.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Low Bank 2
P04F5.description: The control or supply line to the electric catalyst heater on bank 2 is shorted to ground or measures below the expected voltage when the heater is commanded on.

P04F6.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit High Bank 1
P04F6.description: Same as P04F4 with the line shorted to supply or open - the ECU measures higher voltage than the commanded duty cycle allows.

P04F8.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Intermittent Bank 1
P04F8.description: Same as P04F4 with intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault on the heater feed.

P04FA.title: EGR A Control Temperature Too High
P04FA.description: The ECU monitors the operating temperature of the EGR A actuator (or its control electronics).

P04FB.title: Crankcase Ventilation Hose Connection Sensor Range or Performance
P04FB.description: The sensor that monitors PCV hose connection reports a value within plausible range yet inconsistent with the engine model - signal does not switch when the hose is moved during diagnosis, or shows offset against actual hose state.

P04FC.title: Crankcase Ventilation System Performance
P04FC.description: A general performance fault of the crankcase ventilation system - PCV pressure or flow does not match the engine model.

P04FD.title: EGR Actuator A Control Processor Performance
P04FD.description: Modern smart EGR actuators contain their own microcontroller that handles position control internally and reports back over LIN or PWM.

P04FE.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 1
P04FE.description: The catalyst heater on bank 1 is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - measured catalyst light-off time is longer than calibrated.

P04FF.title: Catalyst Heater Circuit Performance Bank 2
P04FF.description: The catalyst heater on bank 2 is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - measured catalyst light-off time is longer than calibrated.

P0500.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Malfunction
P0500.description: The vehicle speed sensor (VSS) signal is missing or implausible.

P0501.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Range/Performance
P0501.description: The VSS signal is present but inconsistent — either values jump implausibly or the sensor reports a speed inconsistent with engine RPM in gear.

P0502.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P0502.description: The primary vehicle speed sensor (VSS A) reports a signal voltage below the plausible lower limit.

P0503.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent Erratic or High
P0503.description: Same as P0502 with the signal noisy, erratic or above the plausible upper limit - typical for a chafed harness, missing reluctor tooth or a sensor with a weakened magnet.

P0504.title: Brake Switch "A"/"B" Correlation
P0504.description: Modern vehicles use two redundant brake switch signals (often one normally-open and one normally-closed).

P0505.title: Idle Air Control System Malfunction
P0505.description: A general fault has been detected in the idle air control (IAC) system.

P0506.title: Idle Air Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
P0506.description: The engine idles below the target RPM despite the IAC opening fully.

P0507.title: Idle Air Control System RPM Higher Than Expected
P0507.description: Idle RPM exceeds the target despite the IAC commanded fully closed.

P0508.title: Idle Air Control System Circuit Low
P0508.description: The control line to the idle air control valve - which opens a small bypass around the throttle to set idle airflow - is shorted to ground or measures a voltage below the plausible level.

P0509.title: Idle Air Control System Circuit High
P0509.description: Same as P0508 with the line shorted to supply or open.

P050A.title: Cold Start Idle Control System Performance
P050A.description: During the cold-start phase the ECU runs an elevated idle speed and a richer mixture to bring the catalyst above light-off temperature quickly.

P050B.title: Cold Start Ignition Timing Performance
P050B.description: During cold-start the ECU retards ignition timing to raise exhaust temperature for catalyst light-off.

P050C.title: Cold Start Engine Coolant Temperature Performance
P050C.description: During cold-start the ECU expects coolant temperature to rise within a calibrated time window.

P050D.title: Cold Start Rough Idle
P050D.description: The ECU detects rough idle behaviour during the cold-start phase only.

P050E.title: Cold Start Engine Exhaust Temperature Too Low
P050E.description: During the cold-start strategy the ECU monitors exhaust temperature to ensure catalyst light-off.

P050F.title: Brake Assist Vacuum Too Low
P050F.description: The ECU monitors the vacuum supplied to the brake booster (either via a dedicated sensor or via intake manifold pressure).

P0510.title: Closed Throttle Position Switch
P0510.description: The dedicated closed-throttle switch (or closed-throttle bit on the TPS) does not behave as expected - either it never activates, never deactivates, or shows incoherent state against TPS voltage and engine load.

P0511.title: Idle Air Control Circuit
P0511.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the idle air control valve - open or short on supply, signal or ground.

P0512.title: Starter Request Circuit
P0512.description: The starter request input - the signal that tells the ECU the driver wants to crank the engine - shows a circuit fault.

P0513.title: Incorrect Immobilizer Key
P0513.description: The immobiliser system has detected a key that is not authorised for this vehicle.

P0514.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P0514.description: The battery temperature sensor reports a value within plausible range yet inconsistent with engine bay or coolant temperature.

P0515.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0515.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the battery temperature sensor - open or short on supply, signal or ground.

P0516.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0516.description: Same as P0515 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P0517.title: Battery Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0517.description: Same as P0515 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P0518.title: Idle Air Control Circuit Intermittent
P0518.description: Same as P0511 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P0519.title: Idle Air Control System Performance
P0519.description: The idle air control system is electrically intact, but the actual idle airflow does not match the commanded value - typical for a sticky valve, intake leak, or carbon build-up around the throttle bore.

P051A.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P051A.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the crankcase pressure sensor A - typically used to monitor PCV operation and detect a clogged separator or disconnected hose.

P051B.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range or Performance
P051B.description: Same as P051A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P051C.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P051C.description: Same as P051A with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P051D.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P051D.description: Same as P051A with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P051E.title: Crankcase Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P051E.description: Same as P051A with intermittent or erratic signal.

P051F.title: PCV Filter Restriction
P051F.description: The pressure or flow sensor in the PCV path detects increased restriction across the oil-mist filter element.

P0520.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A Circuit
P0520.description: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0521.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
P0521.description: The engine oil pressure sensor or switch reports values that are not plausible for current RPM, oil temperature, and engine load.

P0522.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor/Switch Low Voltage
P0522.description: The oil pressure sensor signal is below the expected minimum.

P0523.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch A High
P0523.description: Same as P0520 with the signal voltage above the plausible range - usually a short to supply or sensor failure that pegs the output high.

P0524.title: Engine Oil Pressure Too Low
P0524.description: The ECU has determined that engine oil pressure is below the safe operating threshold.

P0525.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Range or Performance
P0525.description: The control circuit to the cruise control servo (vacuum or electric actuator that holds throttle position) shows feedback in plausible range yet inconsistent with the commanded action - servo slow, sticking, or supply weak.

P0526.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit
P0526.description: A general circuit fault on the cooling fan tachometer feedback - the ECU loses fan speed information needed to verify cooling capacity and detect a stalled or runaway fan.

P0527.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P0527.description: Same as P0526 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the commanded fan speed - typically sensor drift, weak magnet, or partial reluctor damage.

P0528.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0528.description: Same as P0526 with no detectable signal at all - sensor not producing pulses despite the fan being commanded on.

P0529.title: Fan Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0529.description: Same as P0526 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P052A.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P052A.description: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P052B.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
P052B.description: Same as P052A with the phaser stuck retarded - cold-start strategy cannot pull the cam to the advanced position needed for fast catalyst light-off.

P052C.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
P052C.description: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P052D.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2

P052E.title: PCV Regulator Valve Performance
P052E.description: The crankcase ventilation regulator valve - which throttles blow-by gas flow toward the intake based on engine load - is electrically intact but does not deliver the modelled pressure regulation.

P052F.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage
P052F.description: Glow Plug Control Module 1 System Voltage: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0530.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit
P0530.description: General electrical fault on the A/C refrigerant pressure sensor circuit.

P0531.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0531.description: The A/C refrigerant pressure sensor signal is implausible against operating conditions.

P0532.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit Low
P0532.description: A/C pressure sensor signal voltage below the lower threshold — open, short to ground, sensor fault, or a refrigerant charge so low that the pressure is genuinely low.

P0533.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor "A" Circuit High
P0533.description: A/C pressure sensor signal voltage above the upper threshold — short to supply, defective sensor, or a system overcharge/blocked condenser causing genuine high pressure.

P0534.title: A/C Refrigerant Charge Loss
P0534.description: The system detects an abnormally low refrigerant charge.

P0535.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit
P0535.description: The evaporator temperature sensor signal is missing or out of range.

P0536.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P0536.description: The evaporator temperature sensor used to prevent evaporator icing reports a value within plausible range yet not matching the engine model or cabin conditions.

P0537.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0537.description: The evaporator temperature sensor signal voltage is below the lower diagnostic threshold.

P0538.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0538.description: The evaporator temperature sensor signal voltage is above the upper diagnostic threshold.

P0539.title: A/C Evaporator Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0539.description: Same as P0536 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P053A.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Open
P053A.description: The heater on PCV path A - used to prevent ice plugs in the crankcase ventilation hose during cold weather - has an open control circuit.

P053B.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit Low
P053B.description: Same as P053A with the control line shorted to ground.

P053C.title: PCV Heater A Control Circuit High
P053C.description: Same as P053A with the control line shorted to supply.

P053D.title: PCV Heater A Performance
P053D.description: The PCV heater on path A is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - hose temperature does not rise as commanded.

P053E.title: Crankcase Pressure Too High
P053E.description: The crankcase pressure sensor reports a value above the safe upper threshold.

P053F.title: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 1
P053F.description: During cold-start the ECU runs an elevated rail pressure on direct-injection systems for better cold spray atomisation.

P0540.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit
P0540.description: Intake Air Heater A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0541.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Low
P0541.description: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range.

P0542.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit High
P0542.description: Intake Air Heater A Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range.

P0543.title: Intake Air Heater A Circuit Open
P0543.description: The intake air heater (grid heater) on path A - used on cold-start of diesel engines to warm intake air for reliable combustion - has an open control circuit.

P0544.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0544.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 1 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst).

P0545.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Bank 1 Sensor 1 Low
P0545.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor signal at bank 1, sensor 1 is below the lower diagnostic threshold.

P0546.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Bank 1 Sensor 1 High
P0546.description: The exhaust gas temperature sensor signal at bank 1, sensor 1 is above the upper diagnostic threshold.

P0547.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0547.description: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 1: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0548.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0548.description: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 1: the signal voltage is below the expected range.

P0549.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0549.description: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 1: the signal voltage is above the expected range.

P054A.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1
P054A.description: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P054B.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 1
P054B.description: Same as P052B on the B camshaft of bank 1.

P054C.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2
P054C.description: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P054D.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded Bank 2
P054D.description: Same as P052B on the B camshaft of bank 2.

P054E.title: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Lower Than Expected
P054E.description: At idle the ECU expects a calibrated fuel quantity to maintain set-speed.

P054F.title: Idle Control System Fuel Quantity Higher Than Expected
P054F.description: Same as P054E with actual fuel quantity above the model - high friction, sticky throttle, or accessory drag.

P0550.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0550.description: General electrical fault on the power steering pressure sensor.

P0551.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0551.description: The PS pressure sensor signal stays in electrical range but is implausible for the operating state, e.g.

P0552.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Input
P0552.description: PS pressure sensor signal voltage below threshold — open, short to ground, or sensor failure.

P0553.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Circuit High Input
P0553.description: PS pressure sensor signal voltage above threshold — short to supply or sensor failure.

P0554.title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor Intermittent
P0554.description: The power steering pressure sensor signal is intermittent.

P0555.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0555.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the brake booster pressure sensor - the ECU cannot determine vacuum reserve in the booster, which limits the safe operation of stop-start, regenerative-braking blending, and electric vacuum pump control.

P0556.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P0556.description: Same as P0555 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model - drift, partial blockage of the reference port.

P0557.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P0557.description: Same as P0555 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P0558.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P0558.description: Same as P0555 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P0559.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0559.description: Same as P0555 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P055A.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit
P055A.description: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P055B.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Range or Performance
P055B.description: Same as P055A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P055C.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B Low
P055C.description: Same as P055A with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P055D.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor or Switch B High
P055D.description: Same as P055A with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P055E.title: Oxygen Sensor Control Module System Voltage
P055E.description: The dedicated O2 sensor control module - found on systems with a wide-band sensor needing its own pumping current driver - reports its supply voltage outside the calibrated window.

P055F.title: Engine Oil Pressure Out of Range
P055F.description: The measured oil pressure is far outside the expected range for current engine speed and oil temperature - either too low (oil pump weak, oil level low, bearing wear) or anomalously high (relief valve stuck closed, blocked oil cooler).

P0560.title: System Voltage Malfunction
P0560.description: A general fault in the system voltage seen by the ECU — value implausible, missing, or unstable but without crossing the specific thresholds of P0562 (low) or P0563 (high).

P0561.title: System Voltage Unstable
P0561.description: The ECU monitors battery voltage and detects unstable behaviour - rapid fluctuations beyond what current load changes explain.

P0562.title: System Voltage Low
P0562.description: Battery / charging system voltage seen by the ECU has dropped below the lower threshold (typically around 10.5 V).

P0563.title: System Voltage High
P0563.description: Battery / charging system voltage seen by the ECU exceeds the upper threshold (typically around 16 V).

P0564.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit
P0564.description: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0565.title: Cruise Control On Signal
P0565.description: The ECU detects an implausible state of the cruise control on/off signal - either the master switch is stuck on, intermittent, or shows a logic level that does not match other dash signals.

P0566.title: Cruise Control Cancel Input Circuit
P0566.description: Cruise Control Cancel Input Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0567.title: Cruise Control Resume Input Circuit
P0567.description: Cruise Control Resume Input Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0568.title: Cruise Control Set Input Circuit
P0568.description: Cruise Control Set Input Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0569.title: Cruise Control Coast Signal
P0569.description: The coast (decelerate) signal of the cruise control reports an implausible state - typically a stuck or shorted contact.

P056A.title: Cruise Control Increase Distance Signal
P056A.description: Cruise Control Increase Distance Signal: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P056B.title: Cruise Control Decrease Distance Signal
P056B.description: Cruise Control Decrease Distance Signal: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P056C.title: Cruise Control Cancel Signal
P056C.description: The cancel signal (driver-initiated cruise off) reports an implausible state - stuck, missing, or shorted.

P056D.title: Reductant Control Module System Voltage
P056D.description: The reductant (AdBlue) control module reports its supply voltage outside the calibrated window.

P056E.title: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control A Performance
P056E.description: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control A Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P056F.title: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control B Performance
P056F.description: Cold Start Turbocharger Boost Control B Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P0570.title: Cruise Control Accel Signal Malfunction
P0570.description: The cruise control accelerate input signal is implausible — switch contacts welded, wiring fault, or stalk defect.

P0571.title: Brake Switch "A" Circuit Malfunction
P0571.description: The brake light switch signal seen by the ECU is implausible — for example, both contacts active simultaneously, or no signal change despite the brake pedal being pressed (cruise control engages and disengages on this signal).

P0572.title: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit Low
P0572.description: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range.

P0573.title: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit High
P0573.description: Cruise Control/Brake Switch B Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range.

P0574.title: Cruise Control System Vehicle Speed Too High
P0574.description: The cruise control sees actual vehicle speed exceed the set-speed by more than the diagnostic margin (typically going downhill or with throttle override).

P0575.title: Cruise Control Input Circuit
P0575.description: A general circuit fault is detected on a cruise control input that is not specifically multiplexed - typically the dedicated set/resume button input.

P0576.title: Cruise Control Input Circuit Low
P0576.description: Same as P0575 with the input voltage below the plausible range.

P0577.title: Cruise Control Input Circuit High
P0577.description: Same as P0575 with the input voltage above the plausible range.

P0578.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Stuck
P0578.description: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Stuck: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0579.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Range or Performance
P0579.description: Same as P0564 with the analogue level inside the plausible range yet not matching any of the calibrated button levels - resistor ladder drifted, contact resistance increased, or wrong stalk module fitted.

P057A.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Open
P057A.description: The brake pedal position sensor A has an open control circuit.

P057B.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Range or Performance
P057B.description: Same as P057A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the brake-light switch state - typical for a sensor offset against pedal travel or a worn potentiometer track.

P057C.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P057C.description: Same as P057A with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P057D.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P057D.description: Same as P057A with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P057E.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P057E.description: Same as P057A with intermittent or erratic signal.

P057F.title: Battery A State of Charge Performance
P057F.description: The battery monitor reports a State of Charge (SoC) value that does not match the rest-voltage and current pattern - typically a battery near end of life, sulfation, or a deep discharge that the SoC algorithm has not converged on.

P0580.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit Low
P0580.description: Same as P0564 with the analogue input voltage below the plausible range.

P0581.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A Circuit High
P0581.description: Same as P0564 with the analogue input voltage above the plausible range.

P0582.title: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit Open
P0582.description: The vacuum-control solenoid of a vacuum-driven cruise servo (older systems) has an open control circuit - the servo cannot pull the throttle.

P0583.title: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit Low
P0583.description: Same as P0582 with the control line shorted to ground.

P0584.title: Cruise Control Vacuum Control Circuit High
P0584.description: Same as P0582 with the control line shorted to supply.

P0585.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input A and B Correlation
P0585.description: Cruise control uses two redundant multiplexed inputs (A and B) for safety.

P0586.title: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit Open
P0586.description: The vent solenoid of a vacuum-driven cruise servo - which releases vacuum to drop throttle - has an open control circuit.

P0587.title: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit Low
P0587.description: Same as P0586 with the control line shorted to ground.

P0588.title: Cruise Control Vent Control Circuit High
P0588.description: Same as P0586 with the control line shorted to supply.

P0589.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit
P0589.description: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P058A.title: Battery Monitor Module Performance
P058A.description: Battery Monitor Module Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P058B.title: Battery Monitor Module Current Monitoring Performance
P058B.description: Battery Monitor Module Current Monitoring Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P058C.title: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Monitoring Performance
P058C.description: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Monitoring Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P058D.title: Battery Monitor Module Voltage Monitoring Performance
P058D.description: Battery Monitor Module Voltage Monitoring Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P058E.title: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Too High
P058E.description: The battery monitor module measures battery temperature above the safe upper threshold - charging is derated or stopped to prevent thermal runaway.

P058F.title: Battery Monitor Module Temperature Too Low
P058F.description: Same as P058E with the temperature below the safe lower threshold - charging current is reduced to prevent damage to a frozen battery.

P0590.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Stuck
P0590.description: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Stuck: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P0591.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Range or Performance
P0591.description: Same as P0579 on input B.

P0592.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit Low
P0592.description: Same as P0580 on input B.

P0593.title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input B Circuit High
P0593.description: Same as P0581 on input B.

P0594.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Open
P0594.description: The servo motor that drives the cruise control throttle actuator has an open control circuit.

P0595.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Low
P0595.description: Same as P0594 with the control line shorted to ground.

P0596.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit High
P0596.description: Same as P0594 with the control line shorted to supply.

P0597.title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit Open
P0597.description: The map-controlled thermostat - electrically heated to lower its opening temperature on demand for emissions or torque mapping - has an open control circuit.

P0598.title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit Low
P0598.description: Same as P0597 with the control line shorted to ground.

P0599.title: Thermostat Heater Control Circuit High
P0599.description: Same as P0597 with the control line shorted to supply.

P059A.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit
P059A.description: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P059B.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Range or Performance
P059B.description: Same as P059A with feedback in plausible range yet not matching the commanded angle.

P059C.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit High
P059C.description: Same as P059A with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P059D.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit Low

P059E.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent

P059F.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Performance Stuck Off
P059F.description: Active Grille Air Shutter A Performance Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.

P05A0.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Stuck On

P05A1.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Minimum or Maximum Stop Performance
P05A1.description: Active Grille Air Shutter A Position Sensor Minimum or Maximum Stop Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P05A2.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Open
P05A2.description: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Open: the control circuit is open.

P05A3.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Range or Performance
P05A3.description: Same as P05A2 with electrical drive intact but the shutter response not matching the commanded movement - actuator slow or weak.

P05A4.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit High
P05A4.description: Same as P05A2 with the control line shorted to supply.

P05A5.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Control Circuit Low
P05A5.description: Same as P05A2 with the control line shorted to ground.

P05A6.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Supply Voltage Circuit Open
P05A6.description: Active Grille Air Shutter A Supply Voltage Circuit Open: the circuit is open.

P05A7.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P05A7.description: Same as P05A6 with supply voltage below the plausible range.

P05A8.title: Active Grille Air Shutter A Supply Voltage Circuit High
P05A8.description: Same as P05A6 with supply voltage above the plausible range.

P05A9.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Position Sensor Circuit
P05A9.description: Active Grille Air Shutter B Position Sensor Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P05AA.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Position Sensor Range or Performance

P05AB.description: Same as P059C on shutter B.
