P05AD.description: Same as P059E on shutter B.

P05AE.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Performance Stuck Off
P05AE.description: Active Grille Air Shutter B Performance Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.

P05AF.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Stuck On
P05AF.description: Same as P05A0 on shutter B.

P05B0.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Position Sensor Minimum or Maximum Stop Performance
P05B0.description: Active Grille Air Shutter B Position Sensor Minimum or Maximum Stop Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P05B1.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Control Circuit Open
P05B1.description: Active Grille Air Shutter B Control Circuit Open: the control circuit is open.

P05B2.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Control Circuit Range or Performance
P05B2.description: Same as P05A3 on shutter B.

P05B3.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Control Circuit High
P05B3.description: Same as P05A4 on shutter B.

P05B4.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Control Circuit Low
P05B4.description: Same as P05A5 on shutter B.

P05B5.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Supply Voltage Circuit Open
P05B5.description: Active Grille Air Shutter B Supply Voltage Circuit Open: the circuit is open.

P05B6.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P05B6.description: Same as P05A7 on shutter B.

P05B7.title: Active Grille Air Shutter B Supply Voltage Circuit High
P05B7.description: Same as P05A8 on shutter B.

P05B8.title: Restraint Deployment Signal Circuit Open
P05B8.description: The signal line that the restraint control module uses to inform the engine ECU about a deployment event has an open circuit.

P05B9.title: Restraint Deployment Signal Circuit Low
P05B9.description: Same as P05B8 with the signal shorted to ground.

P05BA.title: Restraint Deployment Signal Circuit High
P05BA.description: Same as P05B8 with the signal shorted to supply.

P05BB.title: Restraints Deployed
P05BB.description: The restraint control module reports that one or more airbag or pretensioner stages have been deployed.

P05BC.title: Stop-Start Mode Switch Circuit Open
P05BC.description: The driver-controlled switch that disables stop-start has an open control circuit - the ECU cannot read the driver preference and falls back to the default mode.

P05BD.title: Stop-Start Mode Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P05BD.description: Same as P05BC with the input in plausible range yet not matching the expected toggle behaviour - typically a worn switch contact.

P05BE.title: Stop-Start Mode Switch Circuit Low
P05BE.description: Same as P05BC with the signal shorted to ground.

P05BF.title: Stop-Start Mode Switch Circuit High
P05BF.description: Same as P05BC with the signal shorted to supply.

P05C0.title: Active Grille Air Shutter Module A Over Temperature
P05C0.description: Active Grille Air Shutter Module A Over Temperature: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

P05C1.title: Active Grille Air Shutter Module B Over Temperature
P05C1.description: Active Grille Air Shutter Module B Over Temperature: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip.

P05C2.title: Engine Coolant Pressure Sensor Circuit
P05C2.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the engine coolant pressure sensor - used to detect a pressurised coolant system that has lost pressure (cap, hose, head gasket leak) or is over-pressurised (combustion gases entering coolant).

P05C3.title: Engine Coolant Pressure Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P05C3.description: Same as P05C2 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the expected pressure profile.

P05C4.title: Engine Coolant Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P05C4.description: Same as P05C2 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P05C5.title: Engine Coolant Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P05C5.description: Same as P05C2 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P05C6.title: Engine Coolant Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P05C6.description: Same as P05C2 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P05C7.title: Economy Mode Switch Circuit Open
P05C7.description: The economy-mode (ECO) switch input has an open circuit.

P05C8.title: Economy Mode Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P05C8.description: Same as P05C7 with the input in plausible range yet not matching expected behaviour.

P05C9.title: Economy Mode Switch Circuit Low
P05C9.description: Same as P05C7 with the signal shorted to ground.

P05CA.title: Economy Mode Switch Circuit High
P05CA.description: Same as P05C7 with the signal shorted to supply.

P05CB.title: Vehicle Hardware Incompatibility
P05CB.description: The ECU detects that one or more connected modules report a hardware variant or part number that is not compatible with the current ECU calibration.

P05CC.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 1
P05CC.description: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 1: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P05CD.title: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 2
P05CD.description: Cold Start A Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 2: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P05CE.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 1
P05CE.description: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 1: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P05CF.title: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 2
P05CF.description: Cold Start B Camshaft Position Timing Performance Bank 2: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command.

P05D0.title: Driver Mode Select Switch A Circuit
P05D0.description: Driver Mode Select Switch A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P05D1.title: Driver Mode Select Switch A Circuit Low
P05D1.description: Same as P05D0 with the signal shorted to ground.

P05D2.title: Driver Mode Select Switch A Circuit High
P05D2.description: Same as P05D0 with the signal shorted to supply.

P05D3.title: Driver Mode Select Switch A Range or Performance
P05D3.description: Same as P05D0 with the input in plausible range yet not matching the expected mode pattern - typically a worn switch or analog encoder drift.

P05D4.title: Driver Mode Select Switch B Circuit
P05D4.description: Driver Mode Select Switch B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P05D5.title: Driver Mode Select Switch B Circuit Low
P05D5.description: Same as P05D1 on switch B.

P05D6.title: Driver Mode Select Switch B Circuit High
P05D6.description: Same as P05D2 on switch B.

P05D7.title: Driver Mode Select Switch B Range or Performance
P05D7.description: Same as P05D3 on switch B.

P05D8.title: PCV Regulator Valve Control Circuit Open
P05D8.description: The control circuit of the electrically actuated PCV regulator valve has an open circuit.

P05D9.title: PCV Regulator Valve Control Circuit Low
P05D9.description: Same as P05D8 with the control line shorted to ground.

P05DA.title: PCV Regulator Valve Control Circuit High
P05DA.description: Same as P05D8 with the control line shorted to supply.

P05DB.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Open
P05DB.description: The brake pedal position sensor B has an open control circuit.

P05DC.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Range or Performance
P05DC.description: Same as P057B on sensor B.

P05DD.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P05DD.description: Same as P057C on sensor B.

P05DE.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit High
P05DE.description: Same as P057D on sensor B.

P05DF.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P05DF.description: Same as P057E on sensor B.

P05E0.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A and B Correlation
P05E0.description: Brake-by-wire and electronic brake systems use two redundant pedal position sensors.

P05E1.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P05E1.description: The high-side refrigerant pressure sensor A reports intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault on the sensor that lives close to the compressor.

P05E2.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P05E2.description: The high-side refrigerant pressure sensor B reports intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault on the sensor that lives close to the compressor.

P05E3.title: Park Brake Sensor or Switch Circuit
P05E3.description: The park brake apply switch or position sensor reports a circuit fault.

P05E4.title: Park Brake Sensor or Switch Circuit Low
P05E4.description: Same as P05E3 with the signal shorted to ground.

P05E5.title: Park Brake Sensor or Switch Circuit High
P05E5.description: Same as P05E3 with the signal shorted to supply.

P05E6.title: Park Brake Sensor or Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P05E6.description: Same as P05E3 with input in plausible range yet not matching expected behaviour.

P05E7.title: Park Brake Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P05E7.description: Same as P05E3 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P05E8.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit Open
P05E8.description: The oil bypass valve - which routes oil around the cooler to speed up warm-up - has an open control circuit.

P05E9.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit Low
P05E9.description: Same as P05E8 with the control line shorted to ground.

P05EA.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit High
P05EA.description: Same as P05E8 with the control line shorted to supply.

P05EB.title: Cold Start SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
P05EB.description: Same as P22FF but specifically during the cold-start window - the SCR catalyst inlet temperature does not reach the threshold needed for NOx reduction in the cold-start phase, so reductant injection cannot be enabled.

P05EC.title: Cold Start Injection Timing Performance
P05EC.description: During cold-start the ECU adjusts injection timing (post-injection on diesels, intake-stroke timing on direct-injection petrols) to support catalyst light-off.

P05ED.title: Reductant Heater Control Module Supply Voltage
P05ED.description: The reductant (AdBlue) heater control module - which warms tank, lines and injector to keep AdBlue from freezing - reports its supply voltage outside the calibrated window.

P05EE.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Open
P05EE.description: The supply line that powers the AdBlue dosing pump is open.

P05EF.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P05EF.description: Same as P05EE with the supply voltage below the plausible range.

P05F0.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
P05F0.description: Same as P05EE with the supply voltage above the plausible range.

P05F1.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck On
P05F1.description: The supply relay or driver for the reductant pump is welded or stuck active - the pump runs continuously, even with the engine off, draining the battery and over-pressurising the dosing circuit.

P05F2.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck Off
P05F2.description: Same as P05EE with the supply stuck off - relay does not energise on command.

P05F3.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Open
P05F3.description: The power relay that supplies the entire exhaust aftertreatment system (DOC, DPF, SCR sensors and heaters) reports an open control circuit.

P05F4.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P05F4.description: Same as P05F3 with the control line shorted to ground.

P05F5.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit High
P05F5.description: Same as P05F3 with the control line shorted to supply.

P05F6.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Stuck On
P05F6.description: The aftertreatment power relay is stuck on - aftertreatment electronics stay powered after key-off, draining the battery.

P05F7.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Stuck Off
P05F7.description: Same as P05F3 with the relay not engaging on command.

P05F8.title: Reductant Heater Control Module Performance
P05F8.description: The reductant heater module is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - heater elements aged, supply line resistance, or thermostat sensor offset.

P05F9.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit
P05F9.description: A general circuit fault on the stop-start status signal - the bus or hardwire that tells other modules whether the engine is auto-stopped or running.

P05FA.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit Low
P05FA.description: Same as P05F9 with the signal shorted to ground.

P05FB.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit High
P05FB.description: Same as P05F9 with the signal shorted to supply.

P05FC.title: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 2
P05FC.description: During cold-start the ECU runs an elevated rail pressure on direct-injection systems for better cold spray atomisation.

P05FD.title: Turbocharger Boost Control A Temperature Too High
P05FD.description: The boost control actuator A reports excessive operating temperature - typically heat soak from the turbo housing, prolonged high-load operation, or insufficient cooling.

P05FE.title: Active Grille Air Shutter C Performance Stuck Off
P05FE.description: Active Grille Air Shutter C Performance Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.

P05FF.title: Brake Pressure Sensor and Brake Pedal Position Sensor Correlation
P05FF.description: The brake pressure sensor and pedal position sensor disagree by more than the diagnostic tolerance - one indicates pedal action without the other showing pressure, or vice versa.

P0600.title: Serial Communication Link
P0600.description: A general fault on a serial communication link - typically used by older single-wire diagnostic protocols (KWP2000, ISO 9141) before CAN became universal.

P0601.title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
P0601.description: The ECU's internal memory checksum does not match the expected value at startup — the firmware/calibration in flash has become corrupt.

P0602.title: Control Module Programming Error
P0602.description: The ECU is reporting that it is missing required calibration data — typically appears after a virgin module is installed but never coded/programmed for the vehicle, or after a flash that did not write all blocks.

P0603.title: Internal Control Module Keep Alive Memory (KAM) Error
P0603.description: The ECU detected a fault in its KAM (battery-backed memory used to store adaptations and DTCs).

P0604.title: Internal Control Module Random Access Memory (RAM) Error
P0604.description: ECU self-test detected a RAM fault during runtime checks.

P0605.title: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
P0605.description: ECU self-test detected a ROM/checksum failure on the program memory.

P0606.title: ECM/PCM Processor Fault
P0606.description: The ECU's internal processor self-test has failed.

P0607.title: Control Module Performance
P0607.description: The ECM performs an internal self-test and detects a processor or memory performance fault that does not fit the more specific P0601 to P0606 codes.

P0608.title: Control Module VSS Output A
P0608.description: The vehicle speed signal output from the control module to other systems is faulty.

P0609.title: Control Module VSS Output B
P0609.description: A fault is detected on the secondary vehicle speed signal output (VSS B) that the ECU sends to other modules (instrument cluster, ABS, transmission).

P060A.title: Internal Control Module Monitoring Processor Performance
P060A.description: Modern ECUs have a separate watchdog or monitoring processor that supervises the main processor.

P060B.title: Internal Control Module A and D Processing Performance
P060B.description: The ECU's analog-to-digital converter does not deliver consistent results - typically reference voltage drift, multiplexer fault, or noise on the analog ground.

P060C.title: Internal Control Module Main Processor Performance
P060C.description: The ECU main processor self-diagnosis flagged a performance fault - watchdog, ROM check, or instruction-set self-test failed.

P060D.title: Internal Control Module Accelerator Pedal Position Performance
P060D.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "accelerator pedal position" value.

P060E.title: Internal Control Module Throttle Position Performance
P060E.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "throttle position" value.

P060F.title: Internal Control Module Coolant Temperature Performance
P060F.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine coolant temperature" value.

P0610.title: Control Module Vehicle Options Error
P0610.description: The ECU's stored vehicle option configuration is invalid or does not match the connected hardware.

P0611.title: Fuel Injector Control Module Performance
P0611.description: Modern direct-injection systems use a dedicated injector driver module that generates the high-voltage charge pulses needed to open piezo or solenoid injectors.

P0612.title: Fuel Injector Control Module Relay Control
P0612.description: A circuit fault on the relay that powers the injector driver module - either control line or contact integrity issue.

P0613.title: TCM Processor
P0613.description: The transmission control module performs an internal self-test and detects a processor performance fault.

P0614.title: ECM and TCM Incompatible
P0614.description: The ECM and TCM exchange identification or calibration data over the powertrain bus and detect that they are not a valid pair - typically appears after replacing one of the modules with a unit from a different vehicle variant.

P0615.title: Starter Relay Circuit
P0615.description: General electrical fault on the starter relay control circuit driven by the ECU/PCM.

P0616.title: Starter Relay A Circuit Low
P0616.description: The control line for starter relay A is shorted to ground - the ECU drives the relay and measures voltage too low.

P0617.title: Starter Relay Circuit High
P0617.description: The starter relay control circuit voltage is above the upper threshold — short to supply or stuck driver.

P0618.title: Alternative Fuel Control Module KAM Error
P0618.description: The control module for alternative fuel (CNG, LPG, hydrogen) reports a Keep-Alive-Memory error - persistent calibration values are corrupt or unreadable.

P0619.title: Alternative Fuel Control Module RAM and ROM Error
P0619.description: The alternative fuel control module reports an internal RAM or ROM check failure - module no longer trustworthy.

P061A.title: Internal Control Module Torque Performance
P061A.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine torque" value.

P061B.title: Internal Control Module Torque Calculation Performance
P061B.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "torque calculation" value.

P061C.title: Internal Control Module Engine RPM Performance
P061C.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine speed (RPM)" value.

P061D.title: Internal Control Module Engine Air Mass Performance
P061D.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "intake air mass" value.

P061E.title: Internal Control Module Brake Signal Performance
P061E.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "brake signal" value.

P061F.title: Internal Control Module Throttle Actuator Controller Performance
P061F.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "throttle actuator control" value.

P0620.title: Generator Control Circuit
P0620.description: General electrical fault detected in the alternator/generator control circuit.

P0621.title: Generator Lamp L Control Circuit
P0621.description: The control circuit for the generator warning lamp output (L terminal) reports a fault.

P0622.title: Generator Field F Control Circuit
P0622.description: The control circuit for the generator field terminal (F) reports a fault.

P0623.title: Generator Lamp Control Circuit
P0623.description: Generic generator warning lamp control circuit fault, often used where the lamp terminal designation is not L or where multiple lamps share a single output.

P0624.title: Fuel Cap Lamp Control Circuit
P0624.description: The control circuit for the fuel cap warning lamp reports a fault.

P0625.title: Generator Field Terminal Circuit Low
P0625.description: Voltage on the alternator F terminal (field excitation) is below threshold — open or short to ground in the excitation path.

P0626.title: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit Performance
P0626.description: The generator field circuit response does not match command.

P0627.title: Fuel Pump "A" Control Circuit Open
P0627.description: The ECU detected an open circuit in the fuel pump A control output.

P0628.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low
P0628.description: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low: the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range.

P0629.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High
P0629.description: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High: the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range.

P062A.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Range or Performance
P062A.description: The control output to the primary fuel pump A is electrically intact yet response and fuel pressure response do not match - typically a worn pump, a clogged strainer, or a partially shorted PWM driver.

P062B.title: Internal Control Module Fuel Injector Control Performance
P062B.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "fuel injector control" value.

P062C.title: Internal Control Module Vehicle Speed Performance
P062C.description: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "vehicle speed" value.

P062D.title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 1
P062D.description: The injector driver stage on bank 1 - the high-side or low-side switching transistor that fires the injectors - reports a performance fault.

P062E.title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 2
P062E.description: The injector driver stage on bank 2 - the high-side or low-side switching transistor that fires the injectors - reports a performance fault.

P062F.title: Internal Control Module EEPROM Error
P062F.description: The ECU's EEPROM (persistent calibration storage) reports a check-sum or write error.

P0630.title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible ECM or PCM
P0630.description: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible ECM or PCM: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0631.title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible TCM
P0631.description: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible TCM: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0632.title: Odometer Not Programmed ECM or PCM
P0632.description: The odometer value stored in the ECM/PCM is missing or implausible - typical after a module replacement without odometer programming, or after persistent storage corruption.

P0633.title: Immobiliser Key Not Programmed
P0633.description: The immobiliser system rejects the current key because it is not programmed to this vehicle.

P0634.title: Control Module Internal Temperature A Too High
P0634.description: Control Module Internal Temperature A Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0635.title: Power Steering Control Circuit
P0635.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the power steering control output - typically the line that the ECU uses to request raised idle when steering load is high, or to enable an electric pump.

P0636.title: Power Steering Control Circuit Low
P0636.description: Same as P0635 with the control line shorted to ground.

P0637.title: Power Steering Control Circuit High
P0637.description: Same as P0635 with the control line shorted to supply.

P0638.title: Throttle Actuator Control Range or Performance Bank 1
P0638.description: The drive-by-wire throttle actuator on bank 1 does not respond as commanded - actuator slow, gearing slipping, or position feedback offset against actual blade angle.

P0639.title: Throttle Actuator Control Range or Performance Bank 2
P0639.description: The drive-by-wire throttle actuator on bank 2 does not respond as commanded - actuator slow, gearing slipping, or position feedback offset against actual blade angle.

P063A.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A
P063A.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the alternator voltage sense line A - the line over which the regulator measures battery-side voltage to set charging output.

P063B.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A Range or Performance
P063B.description: Same as P063A with the sense voltage in plausible range yet not matching the alternator output - high contact resistance or wrong calibration.

P063C.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A Low
P063C.description: Same as P063A with the sense voltage below the plausible range.

P063D.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A High
P063D.description: Same as P063A with the sense voltage above the plausible range.

P063E.title: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 1
P063E.description: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P063F.title: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present
P063F.description: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0640.title: Intake Air Heater Control Circuit
P0640.description: A general circuit fault on the intake air heater control - the ECU cannot drive the grid heater at cold-start.

P0641.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Open
P0641.description: The 5 V reference voltage that the ECU supplies to multiple sensors (TPS, MAP, accelerator pedal, etc.) has dropped out or is open-circuit.

P0642.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Low
P0642.description: The 5 V reference voltage on the A circuit (used by multiple sensors) is below threshold — short to ground or excessive current draw by a single sensor pulling the rail down.

P0643.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit High
P0643.description: 5 V reference rail A above threshold — short to a higher voltage source.

P0644.title: Driver Display Serial Communication Circuit
P0644.description: The serial communication line to the driver display (instrument cluster, MIL/check-engine warning) shows a circuit fault.

P0645.title: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit
P0645.description: A general circuit fault on the A/C clutch relay control - the line over which the ECU engages the magnetic clutch to drive the A/C compressor.

P0646.title: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit Low
P0646.description: Same as P0645 with the control line shorted to ground.

P0647.title: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit High
P0647.description: Same as P0645 with the control line shorted to supply.

P0648.title: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit
P0648.description: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.

P0649.title: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit
P0649.description: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.

P064A.title: Fuel Pump Control Module A
P064A.description: A general fault is detected on the dedicated fuel pump control module A.

P064B.title: PTO Control Module

P07B0.description: Transmission Friction Element H Performance/Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.

P07B1.title: Transmission Friction Element H Stuck On
P07B1.description: Transmission Friction Element H Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.

P07B2.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit/Open
P07B2.description: Park position sensor/switch A — confirms that the gear selector lever is in Park, used by shift-by-wire systems and key-interlock logic — is open.

P07B3.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Low
P07B3.description: Park position sensor/switch A reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact.

P07B4.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
P07B4.description: Park position sensor/switch A reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return.

P07B5.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Performance/Low
P07B5.description: Sensor A is electrically intact but its low-end value drifts — for example a value below the calibrated Park threshold while the lever is mechanically out of Park.

P07B6.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Performance High
P07B6.description: Sensor A is electrically intact but the high-end value drifts — for example a value above the calibrated non-Park range while the lever actually is in Park.

P07B7.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P07B7.description: Park position sensor A signal jumps or drops out — typically a worn switch with contact bounce or a loose connector at the shift lever module.

P07B8.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit/Open
P07B8.description: Park position sensor/switch B is the redundant/secondary park-confirmation sensor — used in shift-by-wire systems for safety, so a single sensor failure cannot strand the vehicle in Park or hide a non-Park condition.

P07B9.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Low
P07B9.description: Park sensor/switch B reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact.

P07BA.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit High
P07BA.description: Park sensor/switch B reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P07BB.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Performance/Low
P07BB.description: Sensor B low-end value drifts away from the calibrated Park threshold.

P07BC.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Performance High
P07BC.description: Sensor B high-end value drifts above the calibrated non-Park range.

P07BD.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P07BD.description: Sensor B signal jumps or drops out.

P07BE.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A/B Correlation
P07BE.description: The two redundant park position sensors A and B disagree — one reports Park, the other does not.

P07BF.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P07BF.description: Input/turbine shaft speed sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open supply.

P07C0.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit High
P07C0.description: Sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P07C1.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P07C1.description: Same as sensor A circuit low, applied to sensor B (used in dual-clutch boxes for the second input shaft).

P07C2.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit High
P07C2.description: Same as sensor A circuit high, applied to sensor B.

P07C3.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit Low
P07C3.description: Same as sensor A circuit low, applied to sensor C (used in some heavy-duty or hybrid-coupled transmissions with three input speed sensors).

P07C4.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit High
P07C4.description: Same as sensor A circuit high, applied to sensor C.

P07C5.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P07C5.description: Intermediate shaft speed sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit.

P07C6.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit High
P07C6.description: Intermediate shaft speed sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit.

P07C7.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P07C7.description: Intermediate shaft speed sensor B (second intermediate sensor in dual-clutch boxes) signal voltage below the lower limit.

P07C8.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit High
P07C8.description: Intermediate shaft speed sensor B signal voltage above the upper limit.

P07C9.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit Low
P07C9.description: Intermediate shaft speed sensor C (third intermediate sensor in heavy-duty or hybrid-coupled transmissions) signal voltage below the lower limit.

P07CA.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit High
P07CA.description: Intermediate shaft speed sensor C signal voltage above the upper limit.

P07CB.title: Transmission Fluid Thermostat Performance
P07CB.description: The transmission fluid thermostat (similar in function to a coolant thermostat — opens at a calibrated temperature to route ATF through the cooler) does not regulate temperature within the expected band.

P07CC.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit Low
P07CC.description: Transmission mode switch C input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact.

P07CD.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit High
P07CD.description: Transmission mode switch C input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P07CE.title: Transmission Mode Switch D Circuit
P07CE.description: General electrical fault on the fourth transmission mode select switch input D — additional drive mode beyond C (e.g.

P07CF.title: Transmission Mode Switch D Circuit Low
P07CF.description: Mode switch D input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact.

P07D0.title: Transmission Mode Switch D Circuit High
P07D0.description: Mode switch D input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P07D1.title: Transmission Mode Switch E Circuit
P07D1.description: General electrical fault on the fifth transmission mode select switch input E.

P07D2.title: Transmission Mode Switch E Circuit Low
P07D2.description: Mode switch E input reads stuck low.

P07D3.title: Transmission Mode Switch E Circuit High
P07D3.description: Mode switch E input reads stuck high.

P07D4.title: Transmission Mode Switch F Circuit
P07D4.description: General electrical fault on the sixth transmission mode select switch input F.

P07D5.title: Transmission Mode Switch F Circuit Low
P07D5.description: Mode switch F input reads stuck low.

P07D6.title: Transmission Mode Switch F Circuit High
P07D6.description: Mode switch F input reads stuck high.

P07D7.title: Stuck in Gear 8
P07D7.description: The transmission has entered 8th gear but cannot leave it on command — typically a stuck shift solenoid or a stuck-on friction element holding the 8th-gear pattern locked.

P07D8.title: Unable To Engage Gear 8
P07D8.description: The TCM commands a shift to 8th gear but the gear-ratio measurement does not confirm engagement — friction element does not lock up, slipping clutch, or shift solenoid does not respond.

P07D9.title: Gear 8 Incorrect Ratio
P07D9.description: While in 8th gear, the measured input/output ratio does not match the calibrated value — slipping clutch, wrong gear actually engaged, or speed sensor data wrong.

P07DA.title: 6-7 Shift
P07DA.description: General fault detected during the 6-to-7 upshift event — slipping during the shift, gear-ratio overshoot, or shift completion timeout.

P07DB.title: 7-8 Shift
P07DB.description: General fault detected during the 7-to-8 upshift event.

P07DC.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 1
P07DC.description: Starting from 1st gear, the TCM commanded a specific upshift but the resulting gear ratio matches a different gear.

P07DD.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 2
P07DD.description: Same condition as incorrect shift from gear 1, applied to shifts originating in 2nd gear.

P07DE.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 3
P07DE.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 3rd gear.

P07DF.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 4
P07DF.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 4th gear.

P07E0.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 5
P07E0.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 5th gear.

P07E1.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 6
P07E1.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 6th gear.

P07E2.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 7
P07E2.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 7th gear.

P07E3.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 8
P07E3.description: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 8th gear.

P07E4.title: Unable to Engage Park
P07E4.description: The TCM commands the park pawl to engage but the position sensors do not confirm engagement — typical for shift-by-wire systems where the park actuator (motor or solenoid driving the pawl) is faulty, the cable is broken, or the pawl is jammed against a tooth and cannot drop in.

P07E5.title: Unable to Engage Drive
P07E5.description: TCM commands engagement of Drive but the input/output speed relationship does not match — friction element does not lock up, or the shift solenoid pattern for Drive cannot be commanded.

P07E6.title: Stuck in Park
P07E6.description: The vehicle cannot leave Park even though the operator has commanded a different range.

P07E7.title: Stuck in Drive
P07E7.description: The vehicle cannot leave Drive — typically a stuck shift mechanism, a stuck-on friction element, or a TCM that cannot command the shift to Park or Neutral.

P07E8.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit/Open
P07E8.description: The transmission range control A circuit (used in shift-by-wire to drive the shift actuator that physically positions the manual valve in the valve body) is open.

P07E9.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Performance
P07E9.description: Range control A circuit is electrically intact, but the actuator response does not match the model — for example position feedback that does not move when commanded, or moves slower than expected.

P07EA.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Low
P07EA.description: Range control A circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on.

P07EB.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit High
P07EB.description: Range control A circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return.

P07EC.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit
P07EC.description: General electrical fault on the multi-function transmission range select circuit — used on shift-by-wire systems with rotary or push-button selectors that encode P/R/N/D as a multi-bit pattern.

P07ED.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Stuck
P07ED.description: The multi-function select circuit reports a value that does not change despite operator activity — the rotary encoder is stuck or a push-button is mechanically locked.

P07EE.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Range/Performance
P07EE.description: The multi-function select circuit produces values that do not match any valid bit pattern — multiple positions asserted simultaneously, or values outside the calibrated range.

P07EF.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Low
P07EF.description: Multi-function select circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or pegged at minimum.

P07F0.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit High
P07F0.description: Multi-function select circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or pegged at maximum.

P07F1.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit
P07F1.description: General electrical fault on input/turbine speed sensor C — third input speed sensor in heavy-duty or hybrid-coupled transmissions.

P07F2.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit
P07F2.description: General fault on the communication line between the TCM and a separate transmission range control module (used on systems where the rotary/push-button selector lives in its own intelligent module that talks to the TCM via CAN or LIN).

P07F3.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit Low
P07F3.description: Range control module communication line reads stuck low — bus shorted to ground or one node held the line low continuously.

P07F4.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit High
P07F4.description: Range control module communication line reads stuck high — bus shorted to battery voltage or open at the bus terminator.

P07F5.title: Transmission Range Control Module System Voltage Low
P07F5.description: The range control module reports its supply voltage below the operating threshold — vehicle battery low, charging system underperforming, or supply line resistance excessive.

P07F6.title: Gear 9 Incorrect Ratio
P07F6.description: While in 9th gear, the measured input/output ratio does not match the calibrated value — slipping clutch, wrong gear actually engaged, or speed sensor data wrong.

P07F7.title: Gear 10 Incorrect Ratio
P07F7.description: While in 10th gear, the measured input/output ratio does not match the calibrated value.

P07F8.title: Stuck in Gear 9
P07F8.description: Same condition as stuck in 8th gear, applied to 9th.

P07F9.title: Unable to Engage Gear 9
P07F9.description: Same condition as unable to engage 8th gear, applied to 9th.

P07FA.title: Incorrect Shift From Gear 9
P07FA.description: Same condition as incorrect shift from 8th, applied to 9th.

P07FB.title: Stuck in Gear 10
P07FB.description: Same condition as stuck in 8th, applied to 10th.

P07FC.title: Unable to Engage Gear 10
P07FC.description: Same condition as unable to engage 8th, applied to 10th.

P07FD.title: Incorrect Shift From Gear 10
P07FD.description: Same condition as incorrect shift from 8th, applied to 10th.

P07FE.title: Stuck In Gear - Not Specified
P07FE.description: The TCM detects that the transmission is stuck in some gear but cannot identify which one — typically because multiple input/output ratio cross-checks fail simultaneously, or an early-detection diagnostic fires before the specific-gear detection runs.

P07FF.title: Cold Start Transmission Performance
P07FF.description: During the cold-start phase the transmission does not behave to specification — typically very slow shifts, missed shifts or harsh engagement at low ATF temperature.

P0800.title: Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request)
P0800.description: The transfer case control module has requested the ECM/PCM to illuminate the MIL because of a fault on its side that is emissions- or driveline-relevant.

P0801.title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit
P0801.description: The TCM detects an electrical fault in the reverse inhibit solenoid circuit, which prevents engagement of reverse at high vehicle speeds.

P0802.title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open
P0802.description: The dedicated MIL request line from the TCM to the ECM (used in older systems where modules used a hard wire to ask for the MIL instead of CAN messaging) is open.

P0803.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit
P0803.description: General electrical fault on the upshift/skip-shift solenoid control circuit — used on manual-transmission performance vehicles to force a skip from 1st straight to 4th under low-load cruise (CAFE fuel-economy feature).

P0804.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Lamp Control Circuit
P0804.description: General electrical fault on the upshift/skip-shift indicator lamp control circuit — the dashboard light that prompts the driver to skip from 1st straight to 4th.

P0805.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit
P0805.description: General electrical fault on the clutch position sensor A circuit — used in dual-clutch and automated-manual transmissions to monitor clutch fork or release-bearing position.

P0806.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0806.description: Clutch position sensor A is electrically intact, but its readings drift away from the model — for example the position does not move when the actuator is commanded, or the offset shifts after a thermal cycle.

P0807.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P0807.description: Clutch position sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open reference voltage.

P0808.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit High
P0808.description: Clutch position sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P0809.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0809.description: Clutch position sensor A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, loose connector or oil/heat exposure near the bell housing.

P080A.title: Clutch Position Not Learned
P080A.description: After a clutch replacement or sensor replacement the TCM has not run a successful clutch-position learn cycle.

P080B.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance
P080B.description: Skip-shift solenoid is electrically intact, but the lockout effect does not match commands — solenoid sticks or coil aged, gearbox interlock cannot be applied or released within the expected time.

P080C.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P080C.description: Skip-shift solenoid control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on.

P080D.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit High
P080D.description: Skip-shift solenoid control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil.

P0810.title: Clutch Position Control Error
P0810.description: On automated manual or dual-clutch transmissions, the actual clutch actuator position deviates from commanded position beyond tolerance.

P0811.title: Excessive Clutch A Slippage
P0811.description: The TCM detects more slip across clutch A (the first clutch in dual-clutch boxes, or the launch clutch in automated-manual systems) than the calibration allows.

P0812.title: Reverse Input Circuit
P0812.description: General electrical fault on the reverse-engagement input — the signal that tells the TCM (and other modules — backup lights, parking sensors) that the gear lever is in Reverse.

P0813.title: Reverse Output Circuit
P0813.description: General electrical fault on the reverse-output circuit — the line that drives backup lights, reverse alarm or transfer-case reverse signal.

P0814.title: Transmission Range Display Circuit
P0814.description: General electrical fault on the transmission range display circuit — drives the PRNDL indicator on the dashboard.

P0815.title: Upshift Switch Circuit
P0815.description: The TCM detects an electrical fault on the manual upshift request switch (paddle or +/- lever) circuit.

P0816.title: Downshift Switch Circuit
P0816.description: The TCM detects an electrical fault on the manual downshift request switch circuit.

P0817.title: Starter Disable Circuit/Open
P0817.description: The starter-disable circuit (used by transmission, immobiliser or anti-theft to block cranking unless safety conditions are met — e.g.

P0818.title: Driveline Disconnect Switch Input Circuit
P0818.description: General electrical fault on the driveline disconnect switch input — used on AWD/4WD vehicles to electrically disengage the rear or front axle for fuel economy.

P0819.title: Up and Down Shift Switch to Transmission Range Correlation
P0819.description: The up-shift/down-shift paddle or button input is used in manumatic mode to step through gears, but the inputs only make sense when the gear lever is in Drive or the Manual position.

P081A.title: Starter Disable Circuit Low
P081A.description: Starter disable circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on.

P081B.title: Starter Disable Circuit High
P081B.description: Starter disable circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P081C.title: Park Input Circuit
P081C.description: General electrical fault on the Park input circuit — used by ECM/PCM to know that the gear lever is in Park (allows engine start, raises idle for accessory loads).

P081D.title: Neutral Input Circuit
P081D.description: General electrical fault on the Neutral input circuit — used by ECM/PCM to detect Neutral and adjust idle speed and start enable.

P081E.title: Excessive Clutch B Slippage
P081E.description: Same condition as excessive clutch A slippage, applied to clutch B (second clutch in dual-clutch boxes — the odd-gear clutch typically).

P081F.title: Brake Transmission Shift Interlock (BTSI) Signal Correlation
P081F.description: The Brake Transmission Shift Interlock prevents shifting out of Park unless the brake pedal is pressed.

P0820.title: Gear Lever X-Y Position Sensor Circuit
P0820.description: The TCM detects an out-of-range or implausible signal from the gear lever X-Y position sensor used on shift-by-wire transmissions.

P0821.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit
P0821.description: General electrical fault on the X-axis (left/right) position sensor 1 of an electronic gear lever.

P0822.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit
P0822.description: General electrical fault on the Y-axis (forward/backward) position sensor 1 of an electronic gear lever.

P0823.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0823.description: Gear lever X position sensor 1 signal jumps or drops out — typically a worn rotary contact or vibration on the centre console.

P0824.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0824.description: Gear lever Y position sensor 1 signal jumps or drops out.

P0825.title: Gear Lever Push-Pull Switch (Shift Anticipate)
P0825.description: General electrical fault on the gear-lever push-pull switch — a low-force capacitive or microswitch sensor in the lever knob that detects the operator gripping the lever before it actually moves.

P0826.title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit
P0826.description: The TCM detects a fault in the combined up/down shift switch circuit, where both switch states are simultaneously active or both inactive when activity is expected.

P0827.title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit Low
P0827.description: Up/down shift switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-pressed paddle/button.

P0828.title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit High
P0828.description: Up/down shift switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P0829.title: 5-6 Shift
P0829.description: General fault detected during the 5-to-6 upshift event.

P082A.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance
P082A.description: Gear lever X sensor 1 is electrically intact, but its readings drift outside the calibrated range or do not match the redundant sensor 2.

P082B.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Low
P082B.description: Gear lever X sensor 1 reads stuck low — short to ground or open reference.

P082C.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit High
P082C.description: Gear lever X sensor 1 reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P082D.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance
P082D.description: Gear lever Y sensor 1 is electrically intact, but its readings drift outside the calibrated range.

P082E.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit Low
P082E.description: Gear lever Y sensor 1 reads stuck low — short to ground.

P082F.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit High
P082F.description: Gear lever Y sensor 1 reads stuck high — short to reference voltage.

P0830.title: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit
P0830.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the clutch pedal position switch A used by manual transmission engine control for cruise, start enable and idle correction.

P0831.title: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit Low
P0831.description: Clutch pedal switch A input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact.

P0832.title: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit High
P0832.description: Clutch pedal switch A input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P0833.title: Clutch Pedal Switch B Circuit
P0833.description: General electrical fault on the second clutch pedal switch B — provides redundant clutch-state detection (one switch upper end of pedal travel, other lower end) so the ECM can verify both ends of pedal motion.

P0834.title: Clutch Pedal Switch B Circuit Low
P0834.description: Clutch pedal switch B input reads stuck low.

P0835.title: Clutch Pedal Switch B Circuit High
P0835.description: Clutch pedal switch B input reads stuck high.

P0836.title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit
P0836.description: General electrical fault on the 4WD selector switch input — used by the operator to engage 4WD on demand (4H, 4L, Auto).

P0837.title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P0837.description: 4WD switch is electrically intact but its values do not match a valid bit pattern — multiple positions asserted simultaneously, or values outside the calibrated range.

P0838.title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit Low
P0838.description: 4WD switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact.

P0839.title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit High
P0839.description: 4WD switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P083A.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch G Circuit
P083A.description: General electrical fault on the seventh transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch G circuit.

P083B.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch G Circuit Range/Performance
P083B.description: Pressure sensor G is electrically intact, but the readings do not match the model — drift, jumps or values that do not respond to commanded pressure changes.

P083C.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch G Circuit Low
P083C.description: Pressure sensor G signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open reference.

P083D.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch G Circuit High
P083D.description: Pressure sensor G signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P083E.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch G Circuit Intermittent
P083E.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch G reports a circuit intermittent fault.

P083F.title: Clutch Pedal Switch A/B Correlation
P083F.description: The signals of clutch pedal switches A and B do not correlate within the calibrated tolerance.

P0840.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Range/Performance
P0840.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor A reading is implausible compared to commanded line pressure.

P0841.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Range/Performance
P0841.description: TCM detects rationality fault between fluid pressure sensor A signal and commanded line pressure during defined operating conditions.

P0842.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Low
P0842.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor A circuit reports voltage below threshold, indicating short to ground or sensor failure.

P0843.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
P0843.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor A circuit reports voltage above threshold, indicating short to power or open ground.

P0844.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent
P0844.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch A reports a circuit intermittent fault.

P0845.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit
P0845.description: Electrical fault on the transmission fluid pressure sensor B circuit.

P0846.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit Range/Performance
P0846.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch B reports a circuit range/performance fault.

P0847.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit Low
P0847.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch B reports a circuit low fault.

P0848.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit High
P0848.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch B reports a circuit high fault.

P0849.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent
P0849.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch B reports a circuit intermittent fault.

P084A.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit
P084A.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch H reports a circuit fault.

P084B.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit Range/Performance
P084B.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch H reports a circuit range/performance fault.

P084C.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit Low
P084C.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch H reports a circuit low fault.

P084D.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit High
P084D.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch H reports a circuit high fault.

P084E.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit Intermittent
P084E.description: The transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch H reports a circuit intermittent fault.

P084F.title: Park/Neutral Switch Output Circuit
P084F.description: The park/neutral switch output circuit reports a generic fault.

P0850.title: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit
P0850.description: The ECU detects implausible park/neutral position switch input.

P0851.title: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit Low
P0851.description: Voltage on the park/neutral switch input is below the expected window.

P0852.title: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit High

P0853.title: Drive Switch Input Circuit

P0855.title: Drive Switch Input Circuit High
P0855.description: The drive (D) switch input reports a input circuit high fault.

P0856.title: Traction Control Input Signal

P0857.description: The traction control input signal to the ECM reports a input signal range/performance condition.

P0858.description: The traction control input signal to the ECM reports a input signal low condition.

P085D.description: The gear shift control module A reports a performance fault.

P085E.title: Gear Shift Control Module B Performance
P085E.description: The gear shift control module B reports a performance fault.

P085F.title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P085F.description: The up/down shift switch reports a range/performance fault.
