P249C.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Reductant Injection Control
P249C.description: After cold start the AdBlue injection runs open-loop until SCR temperature is reached.

P249D.title: Closed Loop Reductant Injection Control At Limit Flow Too Low
P249D.description: With reductant injection running closed-loop the controller drives the dosing valve to maximum opening but cannot reach the required AdBlue flow.

P249E.title: Closed Loop Reductant Injection Control At Limit Flow Too High
P249E.description: Same as P249D with the controller fully closing the dosing valve yet still measuring more flow than needed - the valve does not seat fully.

P249F.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Particulate Filter Regeneration Control
P249F.description: The DPF regeneration controller cannot transition into its closed-loop temperature control quickly enough - typically because EGT does not rise to setpoint within the calibrated window.

P24A0.title: Closed Loop Particulate Filter Regeneration Control At Limit Temperature Too Low
P24A0.description: With regeneration running closed-loop the controller is at maximum heat-input demand yet cannot raise EGT to setpoint - typical for a load-poor drive cycle.

P24A1.title: Closed Loop Particulate Filter Regeneration Control At Limit Temperature Too High
P24A1.description: Same as P24A0 with the controller fully reducing heat input yet EGT still rising - typical for a runaway exotherm in the DPF (oil contamination).

P24A2.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 1
P24A2.description: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P24A3.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Bank 2
P24A3.description: The DPF on bank 2 has accumulated soot beyond the normal operating window.

P24A4.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 1
P24A4.description: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P24A5.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Open Bank 1
P24A5.description: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 1 is mechanically stuck in the open (bypassing) position - EGR always bypasses the cooler, gas reaches the intake hotter than designed.

P24A6.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Control Stuck Open Bank 2
P24A6.description: The EGR cooler bypass valve on bank 2 is mechanically stuck in the open (bypassing) position - EGR always bypasses the cooler, gas reaches the intake hotter than designed.

P24A7.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Control Circuit Open
P24A7.description: The dedicated coolant pump for the EGR cooler has an open control circuit - the pump cannot run, EGR cooler temperature rises beyond the safety threshold.

P24A8.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Performance Stuck Off
P24A8.description: The pump is electrically intact but does not deliver flow when commanded - typically a worn impeller or seized rotor.

P24A9.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Control Circuit Low
P24A9.description: Same as P24A7 with the control line shorted to ground.

P24AA.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Control Circuit High
P24AA.description: Same as P24A7 with the control line shorted to supply.

P24AB.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Stuck On
P24AB.description: The pump or its driver is stuck on - the pump runs continuously, even with the engine off, draining battery and bleeding heat from the engine.

P24AC.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Feedback Circuit Low
P24AC.description: The feedback line that confirms pump speed reads below the plausible range - either pump not turning or feedback line shorted to ground.

P24AD.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Feedback Circuit High
P24AD.description: Same as P24AC with the feedback line shorted to supply.

P24AE.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Circuit
P24AE.description: A general circuit fault on the particulate matter (PM) sensor - measures soot in the exhaust downstream of the DPF to verify regeneration.

P24AF.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P24AF.description: Same as P24AE with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P24B0.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Circuit Low
P24B0.description: Same as P24AE with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P24B1.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Circuit High
P24B1.description: Same as P24AE with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P24B2.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P24B2.description: Same as P24AE with intermittent or erratic signal.

P24B3.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Control Circuit Open
P24B3.description: The PM sensor heater (regenerates the sensor by burning off accumulated soot) has an open control circuit.

P24B4.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Control Circuit Range or Performance
P24B4.description: Same as P24B3 with the heater control loop in plausible range yet not matching the heater model.

P24B5.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Control Circuit Low
P24B5.description: Same as P24B3 with the control line shorted to ground.

P24B6.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Control Circuit High
P24B6.description: Same as P24B3 with the control line shorted to supply.

P24B7.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Resistance
P24B7.description: The resistance of the PM sensor heater is outside the calibrated band.

P24B8.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Pressure Sensor Circuit
P24B8.description: A general circuit fault on the LDP internal pressure sensor.

P24B9.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Pressure Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P24B9.description: Same as P24B8 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the pump operating curve.

P24BA.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P24BA.description: Same as P24B8 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P24BB.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P24BB.description: Same as P24B8 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P24BC.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P24BC.description: Same as P24B8 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P24BD.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Switching Valve Control Circuit Open
P24BD.description: The switching valve in the LDP - directs pump output between EVAP test path and reference orifice - has an open control circuit.

P24BE.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Switching Valve Control Circuit Low
P24BE.description: Same as P24BD with the control line shorted to ground.

P24BF.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Switching Valve Control Circuit High
P24BF.description: Same as P24BD with the control line shorted to supply.

P24C0.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Switching Valve Stuck On
P24C0.description: The LDP switching valve is stuck in the activated position.

P24C1.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Switching Valve Performance Stuck Off
P24C1.description: Same as P24C0 with the valve stuck off.

P24C2.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Measurement System Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 1
P24C2.description: The multiple EGT sensors on bank 1 disagree by more than the diagnostic tolerance under stable conditions - one of them has drifted relative to the others.

P24C3.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Measurement System Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 2
P24C3.description: The multiple EGT sensors on bank 2 disagree by more than the diagnostic tolerance under stable conditions - one of them has drifted relative to the others.

P24C4.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Position Sensor Exceeded Learning Limit Bank 1
P24C4.description: The bypass valve position sensor learning has reached its software-side limit on bank 1 - typically heavy soot deposits have shifted the mechanical zero beyond the design adaptation range.

P24C5.title: EGR Cooler Bypass Position Sensor Exceeded Learning Limit Bank 2
P24C5.description: The bypass valve position sensor learning has reached its software-side limit on bank 2 - typically heavy soot deposits have shifted the mechanical zero beyond the design adaptation range.

P24C6.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Temperature Circuit
P24C6.description: A general circuit fault on the temperature element of the PM sensor - used to verify that the sensor is hot enough for measurement after regeneration.

P24C7.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Temperature Circuit Range or Performance
P24C7.description: Same as P24C6 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P24C8.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Temperature Circuit Low
P24C8.description: Same as P24C6 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P24C9.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Temperature Circuit High
P24C9.description: Same as P24C6 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P24CA.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Temperature Circuit Intermittent
P24CA.description: Same as P24C6 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P24CB.title: Reductant Tank Cap Switch Circuit
P24CB.description: A general circuit fault on the AdBlue tank cap switch - reports whether the cap is properly closed.

P24CC.title: Reductant Tank Cap Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P24CC.description: Same as P24CB with input in plausible range yet not matching driver action.

P24CD.title: Reductant Tank Cap Switch Circuit Low
P24CD.description: Same as P24CB with the signal shorted to ground.

P24CE.title: Reductant Tank Cap Switch Circuit High
P24CE.description: Same as P24CB with the signal shorted to supply.

P24CF.title: Reductant Tank Cap Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P24CF.description: Same as P24CB with intermittent or erratic signal.

P24D0.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P24D0.description: The PM sensor supply voltage is below the plausible range.

P24D1.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Regeneration Incomplete
P24D1.description: A sensor regeneration cycle (heating to burn off accumulated soot) did not complete - sensor cannot return to measurement mode.

P24D2.title: Reductant Heater A Sense Circuit
P24D2.description: Reductant Heater A Sense Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P24D3.title: Reductant Heater B Sense Circuit
P24D3.description: Reductant Heater B Sense Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P24D4.title: EGR Cooler Coolant Pump Feedback Circuit
P24D4.description: A general circuit fault on the feedback line that the EGR cooler coolant pump reports speed on.

P24D5.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit
P24D5.description: A general circuit fault on the secondary EVAP system pressure sensor or switch B.

P24D6.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit Range or Performance
P24D6.description: Same as P24D5 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P24D7.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit Low
P24D7.description: Same as P24D5 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P24D8.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit High
P24D8.description: Same as P24D5 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P24D9.title: EVAP System Pressure Sensor or Switch B Circuit Intermittent
P24D9.description: Same as P24D5 with intermittent or erratic signal.

P24DA.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1
P24DA.description: The PM sensor on bank 1 cannot acquire a valid exhaust sample - probe fouled, exhaust path obstructed at sensor, or sensor seal leaking.

P24DB.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Circuit Open
P24DB.description: The secondary reductant purge valve B - which clears AdBlue from injector and lines at shutdown to prevent crystallisation - has an open control circuit.

P24DC.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Performance
P24DC.description: Same as P24DB with the actuator electrically intact yet not delivering the commanded purge flow.

P24DD.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Circuit Low
P24DD.description: Same as P24DB with the control line shorted to ground.

P24DE.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Circuit High
P24DE.description: Same as P24DB with the control line shorted to supply.

P24DF.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Stuck Open
P24DF.description: Purge valve B is mechanically stuck open - AdBlue lines drain continuously, dosing pressure cannot build.

P24E0.title: Reductant Purge Control Valve B Stuck Closed
P24E0.description: Same as P24DF with valve B stuck closed - AdBlue cannot be cleared at shutdown, risk of crystallisation in injector and lines.

P24E1.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit
P24E1.description: A general circuit fault on the NH3 (ammonia) sensor - measures ammonia slip downstream of the SCR catalyst to detect AdBlue overdose.

P24E2.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P24E2.description: Same as P24E1 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P24E3.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit Low
P24E3.description: Same as P24E1 with the signal voltage below the plausible range.

P24E4.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit High
P24E4.description: Same as P24E1 with the signal voltage above the plausible range.

P24E5.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P24E5.description: The ammonia (NH3) slip sensor downstream of the SCR catalyst delivers an intermittent or erratic signal.

P24E6.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit/Open
P24E6.description: The heater inside the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor warms the sensing cell to operating temperature so it can read tailpipe ammonia.

P24E7.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit Low
P24E7.description: The heater control circuit of the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor reads below the expected voltage range.

P24E8.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit High
P24E8.description: The heater control circuit of the NH3 slip sensor reads above the expected voltage range.

P24E9.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit Performance
P24E9.description: The heater of the NH3 slip sensor is electrically intact, but the warm-up profile or steady-state temperature feedback does not match the ECM model.

P24EA.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit
P24EA.description: The supply rail that powers the NH3 slip sensor electronics (typically 5 V or 12 V from the dosing/SCR module) is out of tolerance.

P24EB.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P24EB.description: The NH3 slip sensor supply voltage drops below the lower limit.

P24EC.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit High
P24EC.description: The NH3 slip sensor supply voltage rises above the upper limit.

P24ED.title: NH3 Sensor Calibration Memory
P24ED.description: The NH3 slip sensor stores its individual calibration coefficients in non-volatile memory (EEPROM/flash).

P24EE.title: NH3 Sensor Processor Performance
P24EE.description: The microcontroller inside the smart NH3 slip sensor reports an internal performance fault — failed self-test, watchdog reset, or out-of-range plausibility checks.

P24EF.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit/Open
P24EF.description: The wake-up line that brings a sleeping ECU back from low-power mode is open.

P24F0.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit Low
P24F0.description: The wake-up input on the control module reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted wake signal.

P24F1.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit High
P24F1.description: The wake-up input reads above the expected range — typically a short to battery voltage.

P24F2.title: EGR Temperature/Charge Air Cooler Temperature Correlation
P24F2.description: After a long key-off soak both the EGR temperature sensor and the charge-air cooler outlet temperature sensor must read approximately the same ambient temperature.

P24F3.title: Reductant Tank Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
P24F3.description: After a long key-off soak the AdBlue/DEF tank temperature and the fuel tank temperature should read close to each other (both at ambient).

P24F4.title: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P24F4.description: The pre-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level — for example after a fuel cut or transition into low-load.

P24F5.title: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
P24F5.description: The post-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 2) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level.

P24F6.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Open
P24F6.description: On systems that inject HC dosing fuel or AIR-assisted reductant into the aftertreatment, a purge valve clears the line after each dosing event.

P24F7.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Closed
P24F7.description: The aftertreatment HC dosing or reductant purge valve is stuck closed.

P24F8.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit
P24F8.description: General electrical fault in the control circuit of the aftertreatment fuel/air purge valve.

P24F9.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Range/Performance
P24F9.description: The valve coil is electrically intact, but the response (current rise time, return-current decay, position feedback) does not match the ECM model.

P24FA.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Low
P24FA.description: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a failed low-side driver.

P24FB.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit High
P24FB.description: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage or an open ground/return path.

P24FC.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P24FC.description: The PM (soot) sensor heater is driven by a current-limited stage so it can burn off accumulated soot before each measurement.

P24FD.title: Particulate Filter A Incorrect
P24FD.description: The ECM identifies the installed particulate filter A as the wrong part — backpressure signature, regeneration efficiency or coded part-number do not match the application.

P24FE.title: SCR Catalyst Incorrect
P24FE.description: The ECM identifies the installed SCR catalyst as the wrong part — NOx conversion efficiency, NH3 storage capacity or coded part-number do not match the expected application.

P24FF.title: Reductant Temperature Too High
P24FF.description: The temperature of the AdBlue/DEF in the dosing system exceeds the safe limit — risk of thermal decomposition (NH3/biuret formation) and clogged dosing nozzles.

P2500.title: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit Low
P2500.description: The L-terminal feedback line from the alternator (charging warning lamp circuit) reads below the lower limit.

P2501.title: Generator Lamp/L-Terminal Circuit High
P2501.description: The L-terminal feedback from the alternator reads above the upper limit — short to supply or open ground side.

P2502.title: Charging System Voltage
P2502.description: The ECU detects an out-of-range charging system voltage without specifying high or low.

P2503.title: Charging System Voltage Low
P2503.description: The ECU detects that battery voltage during operation stays below the regulated target.

P2504.title: Charging System Voltage High
P2504.description: The ECU detects a battery voltage above the regulated upper limit.

P2505.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal
P2505.description: The ECM/PCM monitors the main switched battery feed (typically terminal 15 / ignition-switched supply via the main relay).

P2506.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Range/Performance
P2506.description: The switched-battery input to the ECM/PCM is present, but the level or transient behaviour is out of plausibility — sagging during cranking, slow ramp-up after main-relay close, or noisy.

P2507.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Low
P2507.description: The ECM/PCM switched-battery input reads below threshold while the ignition is on.

P2508.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal High
P2508.description: The ECM/PCM switched-battery input reads above the upper threshold.

P2509.title: ECM/PCM Power Input Signal Intermittent
P2509.description: The ECU detects sporadic interruptions of its supply voltage.

P250A.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit
P250A.description: General electrical fault on the engine oil level sensor circuit.

P250B.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P250B.description: The oil level sensor is electrically intact, but the level reading is implausible — for example a constant value across drives, jumps that cannot match real oil consumption, or readings outside the design range.

P250C.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Low
P250C.description: The oil level sensor signal voltage reads below the lower limit, typically a short to ground or an open at the reference end of the sender.

P250D.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit High
P250D.description: The oil level sensor signal voltage reads above the upper limit, typically a short to reference voltage or an open signal return.

P250E.title: Engine Oil Level Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P250E.description: The oil level signal jumps or drops out intermittently — usually loose contacts, vibration cracks at the sender or oil sloshing on bumpy roads.

P250F.title: Engine Oil Level Too Low
P250F.description: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level below the safe minimum after sensor checks pass.

P2510.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2510.description: The voltage reported on the main power relay sense line for the engine controller does not match expectation.

P2511.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Intermittent
P2511.description: The sense (feedback) line that lets the ECM verify the main power relay has actually closed shows intermittent dropouts.

P2512.title: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit/Open
P2512.description: The Event Data Recorder (EDR / black box) request line — used by the ECM or restraint module to trigger the EDR to capture pre-crash data — is open.

P2513.title: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit Low
P2513.description: The EDR request line reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently asserted request.

P2514.title: Event Data Recorder Request Circuit High
P2514.description: The EDR request line reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage.

P2515.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P2515.description: General electrical fault in the second A/C refrigerant pressure sensor circuit.

P2516.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2516.description: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B is electrically intact, but its reading does not match the system model — for example pressures that do not fall when the compressor is off, do not change with ambient temperature, or contradict pressure sensor A.

P2517.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P2517.description: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B signal voltage reads below the lower limit.

P2518.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P2518.description: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor B signal voltage reads above the upper limit.

P2519.title: A/C Request A Circuit
P2519.description: General electrical fault on the A/C compressor request input A.

P251A.title: PTO Enable Switch Circuit/Open
P251A.description: The Power Take-Off (PTO) enable switch input to the ECM is open.

P251B.title: PTO Enable Switch Circuit Low
P251B.description: The PTO enable switch input reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently closed switch.

P251C.title: PTO Enable Switch Circuit High
P251C.description: The PTO enable switch input reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage.

P251D.title: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit/Open
P251D.description: The PTO engine-shutdown command line is open.

P251E.title: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit Low
P251E.description: The PTO engine-shutdown command line reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted shutdown request.

P251F.title: PTO Engine Shutdown Circuit High
P251F.description: The PTO engine-shutdown command line reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage.

P2520.title: A/C Request A Circuit Low
P2520.description: The A/C compressor request input A reads stuck low — typically a short to ground or a permanently asserted request.

P2521.title: A/C Request A Circuit High
P2521.description: The A/C request input A reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage.

P2522.title: A/C Request B Circuit
P2522.description: General electrical fault on the second A/C request input B.

P2523.title: A/C Request B Circuit Low
P2523.description: The A/C request input B reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently asserted request.

P2524.title: A/C Request B Circuit High
P2524.description: The A/C request input B reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage.

P2525.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2525.description: General electrical fault on the vacuum reservoir pressure sensor circuit.

P2526.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2526.description: The vacuum reservoir pressure sensor is electrically intact, but the reading does not match the model — vacuum that does not build up after pump activation, does not bleed off when consumers draw, or stays at one value.

P2527.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2527.description: Sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — usually a short to ground or open reference.

P2528.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2528.description: Sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — usually a short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P2529.title: Vacuum Reservoir Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P2529.description: The sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — loose connector, vibration, or chafed harness.

P252A.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit
P252A.description: General electrical fault on the engine oil quality sensor — typically a capacitive/dielectric sensor that estimates oil aging from permittivity, viscosity proxies and conductivity.

P252B.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P252B.description: The oil quality sensor is electrically intact, but the readings do not match the model — for example permittivity that does not change after an oil change, or shifts inconsistent with km/h driven.

P252C.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Low
P252C.description: Sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — typically a short to ground in the signal line or an internal short across the sensor electrode.

P252D.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit High
P252D.description: Sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — typically a short to reference voltage or an open signal return.

P252E.title: Engine Oil Quality Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P252E.description: The oil quality sensor signal jumps or drops out — usually a loose connector at the oil pan, an oil-soaked harness or vibration cracks at the sensor housing.

P252F.title: Engine Oil Level Too High
P252F.description: The oil level monitor reports the engine oil level above the safe maximum after sensor checks pass.

P2530.title: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit
P2530.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the ignition switch run position input.

P2531.title: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit Low
P2531.description: The ignition switch Run-position input reads stuck low — short to ground or a permanently closed contact.

P2532.title: Ignition Switch Run Position Circuit High
P2532.description: The ignition switch Run-position input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return.

P2533.title: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit
P2533.description: General electrical fault on the ignition switch On/Start (terminal 50 / crank) input.

P2534.title: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit Low
P2534.description: The On/Start input reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently closed contact.

P2535.title: Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit High
P2535.description: The On/Start input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P2536.title: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit
P2536.description: General electrical fault on the ignition switch accessory (terminal 75 / ACC) input.

P2537.title: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit Low
P2537.description: The ACC input reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently closed contact.

P2538.title: Ignition Switch Accessory Position Circuit High
P2538.description: The ACC input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P2539.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit
P2539.description: General electrical fault on the low-pressure fuel system sensor — typically the lift-pump or pre-supply pressure sensor that monitors the rail feeding the high-pressure pump.

P253A.title: PTO Sense Circuit/Open
P253A.description: The PTO sense (engagement feedback) line is open.

P253B.title: PTO Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P253B.description: The PTO sense circuit is electrically intact, but the engagement feedback does not match the command.

P253C.title: PTO Sense Circuit Low
P253C.description: The PTO sense input reads stuck low — short to ground or limit switch stuck closed.

P253D.title: PTO Sense Circuit High
P253D.description: The PTO sense input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return.

P253E.title: PTO Sense Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P253E.description: The PTO sense signal jumps or drops out — usually loose connectors, a chattering limit switch, or vibration on the work attachment.

P253F.title: Engine Oil Deteriorated
P253F.description: The oil quality monitor concludes that the engine oil has reached the end of its useful life — based on permittivity, soot content, fuel dilution and total operating hours.

P2540.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit
P2540.description: The ECU detects a general fault in the low-pressure fuel system pressure sensor circuit.

P2541.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2541.description: The signal of the low-pressure fuel sensor does not match the expected value during operation.

P2542.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Sensor Circuit High
P2542.description: The low-pressure fuel system sensor signal voltage is above the upper limit.

P2543.title: Power Demand Signal Circuit
P2543.description: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the power demand input signal used to coordinate accessory loads (e.g.

P2544.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A
P2544.description: The ECU detects an invalid torque-management request signal A from another control unit (e.g.

P2545.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A Range/Performance
P2545.description: The ECM receives torque-management requests from other modules (TCM during shifts, ABS/ESC during traction events, hybrid controller).

P2546.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A Low
P2546.description: Torque management input A reads stuck low — analog short to ground or message stuck at minimum value.

P2547.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal A High
P2547.description: Torque management input A reads stuck high — analog short to reference voltage or message stuck at maximum value.

P2548.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B
P2548.description: General electrical fault on the second torque-management request input B.

P2549.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B Range/Performance
P2549.description: Input B is electrically intact but the values are implausible — same failure mode as the A-side performance fault, applied to the second torque-management channel.

P254A.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit/Open
P254A.description: The PTO speed-selector switch 1 input is open.

P254B.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Range/Performance
P254B.description: The selector input is electrically intact but the value is implausible — multiple positions asserted at once, or a value that cannot map to any of the configured speed presets.

P254C.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit Low
P254C.description: PTO speed selector 1 input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal pegged at minimum.

P254D.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit High
P254D.description: PTO speed selector 1 input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal pegged at maximum.

P254E.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P254E.description: The PTO speed selector signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration on the work attachment.

P254F.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit
P254F.description: General electrical fault on the engine hood (bonnet) switch circuit.

P2550.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B Low
P2550.description: Torque management input B reads stuck low — short to ground or message at minimum.

P2551.title: Torque Management Request Input Signal B High
P2551.description: Torque management input B reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or message at maximum.

P2552.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit
P2552.description: General electrical fault on the throttle/fuel inhibit input A.

P2553.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit Range/Performance
P2553.description: The throttle/fuel inhibit A signal is electrically intact but its value does not match the system context — for example asserted while the immobilizer reports OK, or de-asserted while a hybrid HV interlock is active.

P2554.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit Low
P2554.description: Throttle/fuel inhibit A reads stuck low — short to ground or permanently asserted.

P2555.title: Throttle/Fuel Inhibit A Circuit High
P2555.description: Throttle/fuel inhibit A reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P2556.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit
P2556.description: General electrical fault on the engine coolant level sensor/switch circuit.

P2557.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P2557.description: The coolant level sensor is electrically intact, but the readings are implausible — for example a level that does not move at all over many drive cycles, or jumps that cannot match real coolant loss.

P2558.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P2558.description: Coolant level sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or internal short.

P2559.title: Engine Coolant Level Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P2559.description: Coolant level sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P255A.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit/Open
P255A.description: The second PTO speed-selector switch input is open.

P255B.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Range/Performance
P255B.description: PTO speed selector switch 2 is electrically intact but its value does not match a valid bit pattern — multiple positions asserted, or values that do not map to any preset.

P255C.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit Low
P255C.description: PTO speed selector 2 input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal pegged at minimum.

P255D.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit High
P255D.description: PTO speed selector 2 input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal pegged at maximum.

P255E.title: PTO Speed Selector Sensor/Switch 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P255E.description: PTO speed selector 2 signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration on the work attachment.

P255F.title: A/C Request A Circuit Range/Performance
P255F.description: The A/C request input A is electrically intact, but its value does not match the system context — for example asserted while the HVAC controller reports off, toggling rapidly, or sustained while compressor pressures cannot support it.

P2560.title: Engine Coolant Level Low
P2560.description: The coolant level monitor reports the engine coolant below the safe minimum after sensor checks pass.

P2561.title: A/C Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P2561.description: The A/C / HVAC control module has requested the ECM to illuminate the malfunction indicator (MIL) because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side.

P2562.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit
P2562.description: General electrical fault on the turbocharger boost control position sensor A — the feedback sensor on the wastegate or VGT actuator (often a contactless Hall sensor).

P2563.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit
P2563.description: The position feedback sensor on the variable-geometry or wastegate turbocharger actuator is not communicating or is implausible.

P2564.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P2564.description: Position sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground in the signal line or open reference voltage at the sensor.

P2565.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Circuit High
P2565.description: Position sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage in the signal line or open signal return.

P2566.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Range/Performance
P2566.description: The turbocharger actuator position sensor reports a value, but it does not track commanded vane or wastegate position within tolerance.

P2567.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit Low
P2567.description: The turbocharger position sensor signal is below the lower limit — short to ground or sensor at zero stop.

P2568.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit High
P2568.description: The turbocharger position sensor signal is above the upper limit — short to supply, open ground or sensor failed high.

P2569.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P2569.description: Direct Ozone Reduction (DOR) catalysts are coated radiator surfaces or dedicated catalysts that decompose tropospheric ozone passing over the radiator — used for low-emissions vehicles.

P256A.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit/Open
P256A.description: The idle-speed selector input is open.

P256B.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Range/Performance
P256B.description: The idle-speed selector input is electrically intact but the value does not match a valid preset — multiple positions or a non-mappable value.

P256C.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit Low
P256C.description: Idle-speed selector input reads stuck low — short to ground or analog signal at minimum.

P256D.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit High
P256D.description: Idle-speed selector input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or analog signal at maximum.

P256E.title: Engine Idle Speed Selector Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P256E.description: The idle-speed selector signal jumps or drops out — usually a worn rotary contact or vibration.

P256F.title: A/C Request B Circuit Range/Performance
P256F.description: A/C request input B is electrically intact but its value does not match the system context — same failure mode as the input A performance fault, applied to the second HVAC channel.

P2570.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P2570.description: The DOR catalyst temperature sensor reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P2571.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2571.description: The DOR catalyst temperature sensor signal jumps or drops out — typically loose connectors or chafed wiring near the radiator pack.

P2572.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit
P2572.description: General electrical fault on the DOR catalyst deterioration sensor circuit.

P2573.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2573.description: The DOR deterioration sensor is electrically intact but its readings drift or do not match the model — for example a deterioration value that does not move with km/h driven, or moves implausibly fast.

P2574.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Low
P2574.description: The DOR deterioration sensor signal voltage reads below the lower limit — short to ground or internal short.

P2575.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit High
P2575.description: The DOR deterioration sensor signal voltage reads above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P2576.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Deterioration Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2576.description: The DOR deterioration sensor signal jumps or drops out — typically loose connectors or chafed wiring near the radiator.

P2577.title: Direct Ozone Reduction Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold
P2577.description: The DOR catalyst no longer reduces tropospheric ozone with the required efficiency, based on the deterioration sensor and operating-time model.

P2578.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit
P2578.description: General electrical fault on the turbocharger/supercharger shaft speed sensor A — a high-frequency Hall or eddy-current sensor on the compressor shaft.

P2579.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P2579.description: Turbo speed sensor A is electrically intact, but the speed reading does not match the model — for example a speed that does not climb when boost rises, drifts away from the air-mass-flow estimate, or jumps.

P257A.title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit/Open
P257A.description: The control circuit that drives the vacuum reservoir control valve (or vacuum pump motor) is open.

P257B.title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit Low
P257B.description: The vacuum reservoir control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on.

P257C.title: Vacuum Reservoir Control Circuit High
P257C.description: The vacuum reservoir control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil.

P257D.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P257D.description: The hood switch is electrically intact, but its state is implausible — for example reporting hood-open while vehicle speed is rising, or rapid toggles.

P257E.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit Low
P257E.description: The hood switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed switch.

P257F.title: Engine Hood Switch Circuit High
P257F.description: The hood switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return.

P2580.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P2580.description: Turbo speed sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground in the signal line or open supply.

P2581.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit High
P2581.description: Turbo speed sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P2582.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P2582.description: Turbo speed sensor A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, oil mist on the sensor tip, or chafed wiring near the hot turbo.

P2583.title: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Single Sensor or Center
P2583.description: General fault on the radar/lidar/camera distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise control.

P2584.title: Fuel Additive Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P2584.description: The fuel additive control module — typical for diesel cars with a separate Eolys/Cerine additive tank that aids DPF regeneration — has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side.

P2585.title: Fuel Additive Control Module Warning Lamp Request
P2585.description: The fuel additive control module asks for the additive-low warning lamp to be illuminated — the additive tank (Eolys/Cerine, used to lower DPF regen temperature) is approaching empty or has reached a service threshold.

P2586.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit
P2586.description: General electrical fault on the turbocharger boost control position sensor B — second position sensor on the same actuator (redundant Hall) or on a second turbo (twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage).

P2587.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2587.description: Position sensor B is electrically intact, but the reading does not track sensor A or the actuator-command model.

P2588.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P2588.description: Position sensor B signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open reference.

P2589.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit High
P2589.description: Position sensor B signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P258A.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A/Open
P258A.description: The control circuit driving the electric vacuum pump (used to maintain brake-booster vacuum on direct-injection or hybrid powertrains where the engine is not always running) is open.

P258B.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A Range/Performance
P258B.description: The vacuum pump control circuit is electrically intact, but the pump response does not match the model — pump runs longer than expected to reach setpoint, current draw rises (mechanically tight) or vacuum does not build at all.

P258C.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A Low
P258C.description: The electric vacuum pump control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on.

P258D.title: Vacuum Pump Control Circuit A High
P258D.description: The vacuum pump control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return.

P258E.title: PTO Enable Switch Performance
P258E.description: The PTO enable switch is electrically intact but its state does not match operating conditions — for example asserted while the vehicle is rolling above the PTO speed limit, or asserted/de-asserted in fast succession.

P258F.title: Torque Management Request Output Signal
P258F.description: The ECM/PCM produces a torque-management output signal for downstream consumers (TCM during shifts, hybrid module, transfer case) and detects a fault on this output — open, short, or feedback voltage outside expected range.

P2590.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P2590.description: Position sensor B signal jumps or drops out — vibration on the actuator, oil mist contamination or chafed wiring near the hot turbo.

P2591.title: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Left
P2591.description: General fault on the left-side front distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise.

P2592.title: Cruise Control Front Distance Range Sensor Right
P2592.description: General fault on the right-side front distance-range sensor used by adaptive cruise.

P2593.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit
P2593.description: General electrical fault on the second turbocharger speed sensor B — used on twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage installations to read the second compressor shaft speed.

P2594.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P2594.description: Turbo speed sensor B is electrically intact, but the speed reading does not match the boost or air-mass model — same failure mode as sensor A performance fault, applied to the second turbo.

P2595.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P2595.description: Turbo speed sensor B signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open supply.

P2596.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit High
P2596.description: Turbo speed sensor B signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.

P2597.title: Turbocharger Speed Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2597.description: Turbo speed sensor B signal jumps or drops out — vibration, oil mist or chafed wiring at the second turbo.

P2598.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Performance - Stuck Low
P2598.description: Position sensor A reports a value stuck near the low end of its travel even when the actuator is commanded to move.

P2599.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor A Performance - Stuck High
P2599.description: Position sensor A reports a value stuck near the high end of its travel — actuator stuck open (wastegate held wide open, VGT vanes seized at maximum opening) or sensor pegged high.

P259A.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Performance - Stuck Low
P259A.description: Same condition as the A-side stuck-low fault, but on the second sensor / second turbo.

P259B.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor B Performance - Stuck High
P259B.description: Same as the A-side stuck-high fault, applied to sensor B / turbo B.

P259C.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Turbocharger A Boost Control
P259C.description: After start-up the boost-control loop on turbo A takes longer than the calibration limit to transition from open-loop to closed-loop control.

P259D.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Turbocharger B Boost Control
P259D.description: Same condition as the turbo A excessive-warm-up fault, applied to the second turbo.

P259E.title: Turbocharger A Boost Control Position At Low Limit
P259E.description: The boost-control actuator on turbo A has been operating at the low end of its travel for too long — the closed-loop controller is saturated against the lower stop trying to reach the boost setpoint.

P259F.title: Turbocharger A Boost Control Position At High Limit
P259F.description: The boost-control actuator on turbo A has been operating at the high end of its travel — the controller is saturated against the upper stop trying to bleed off boost.

P25A0.title: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At Low Limit
P25A0.description: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At Low Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P25A1.title: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At High Limit
P25A1.description: Turbocharger B Boost Control Position At High Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P25A2.title: Brake System Control Module A Requested MIL Illumination
P25A2.description: The primary brake system control module (ABS/ESC/iBooster) has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side — for example a regenerative braking fault on a hybrid that affects driveline torque flow.

P25A3.title: Engine Hood Open
P25A3.description: After plausibility checks the body controller has concluded that the engine hood is genuinely open while the vehicle is operating.

P25A4.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit
P25A4.description: General electrical fault on the fuel mode select switch — used on bi-fuel vehicles (CNG/LPG/H2/gasoline) so the driver can pick the active fuel.

P25A5.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Performance
P25A5.description: The fuel mode select switch is electrically intact, but its state does not match operating conditions — switched to gas while gas tank is empty, or fast toggling.

P25A6.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit Low
P25A6.description: Fuel mode switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact.

P25A7.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit High
P25A7.description: Fuel mode switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P25A8.title: Fuel Mode Select Switch Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P25A8.description: Fuel mode switch signal jumps or drops out — worn contact or vibration.

P25A9.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit/Open
P25A9.description: The piston-cooling oil-jet control circuit is open.

P25AA.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Low
P25AA.description: The piston-cooling oil-jet control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on.

P25AB.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit High
P25AB.description: Control circuit stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return.

P25AC.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P25AC.description: The control circuit is electrically intact, but the solenoid valve does not open when commanded — confirmed by oil-pressure or oil-temperature feedback that does not change after the activation pulse.

P25AD.title: Piston Cooling Oil Control Circuit Stuck On
P25AD.description: The piston cooling solenoid does not close when commanded off — jets remain active when not needed.

P25AE.title: Piston Cooling Oil Pressure Too Low
P25AE.description: With the piston-cooling jets commanded on, the dedicated oil-pressure sensor in that gallery reads below the safe threshold.

P25AF.title: Coolant Temperature Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P25AF.description: A dedicated coolant-temperature control module (used on engines with electric coolant pumps and electronic thermostats to keep the cylinder head and block at independent setpoints) has requested the ECM to illuminate the MIL because of an emissions-relevant fault on its side.

P25B0.title: Fuel Level Sensor A Stuck
P25B0.description: Fuel level sensor A (typically the float in the main fuel tank section) reports a value that does not change over a long driving distance — the float is mechanically stuck against the tank wall, baffle or pump module.

P25B1.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Stuck
P25B1.description: Same condition as sensor A stuck, applied to the second fuel level sensor B.

P25B2.title: Fuel Level Sensor A or B Stuck
P25B2.description: The ECM detects that one of the two level sensors is stuck but cannot identify which from the available signals — for example because the saddle-tank algorithm sees implausible delta only intermittently.

P25B3.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate A Stuck Open
P25B3.description: Wastegate A is mechanically stuck open.

P25B4.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate A Stuck Closed
P25B4.description: Wastegate A is mechanically stuck closed.

P25B5.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate B Stuck Open
P25B5.description: Same as wastegate A stuck open, applied to the second wastegate (twin-turbo, sequential or two-stage).

P25B6.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate B Stuck Closed
P25B6.description: Same as wastegate A stuck closed, applied to the second wastegate.

P25B7.title: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit
P25B7.description: General electrical fault on the auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input.

P25B8.title: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit Low
P25B8.description: Auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact.

P25B9.title: Auxiliary Ignition Switch On/Start Position Circuit High
P25B9.description: Auxiliary ignition switch On/Start input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P25BA.title: Regeneration Control Switch Circuit/Open
P25BA.description: The DPF/SCR forced-regeneration request switch — used on commercial vehicles to let the operator force a parked regeneration when the automatic regen has been postponed too often — is open.

P25BB.title: Regeneration Control Switch Circuit Low
P25BB.description: Regeneration control switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact.

P25BC.title: Regeneration Control Switch Circuit High
P25BC.description: Regeneration control switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage.

P25BD.title: Unmetered Fuel - Forced Engine Shutdown
P25BD.description: The engine controller commanded a forced shutdown after detecting unmetered fuel reaching the combustion chambers.

P25BE.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit / Open
P25BE.description: The controller cannot drive the alternative-fuel disable line that switches a bi-fuel vehicle (CNG, LPG, hydrogen) back to gasoline.

P25BF.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit High
P25BF.description: Voltage on the alternative-fuel disable control line is above the expected window.

P25C0.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Control Circuit Low
P25C0.description: Voltage on the alternative-fuel disable control line is below the expected window.

P25C1.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit
P25C1.description: The feedback signal that confirms the alt-fuel disable command was carried out is missing or out of range.

P25C2.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit High
P25C2.description: The disable feedback signal sits above its valid window.

P25C3.title: Alternative Fuel Disable Signal Circuit Low
P25C3.description: The disable feedback signal sits below its valid window.

P25C4.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P25C4.description: The temperature sensor monitoring the electric brake booster (iBooster, eBooster) returns no usable signal.

P25C5.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P25C5.description: The booster temperature sensor reading is implausible relative to commanded assist or coolant temperature.

P25C6.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P25C6.description: The booster temperature signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold.

P25C7.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P25C7.description: The booster temperature signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold.

P25C8.title: Brake Booster Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P25C8.description: The booster temperature signal jumps or drops out for short moments.

P25C9.title: Brake System Control Module B Requested MIL Illumination
P25C9.description: A second brake system control module (typically the redundant secondary unit on by-wire or AV-grade brake systems) has signalled an emissions-relevant fault and requested the engine controller to switch on the MIL.

P25CA.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P25CA.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the intake camshaft phaser on bank 1 in its base position at engine off.

P25CB.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P25CB.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is below the expected voltage window.

P25CC.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 1
P25CC.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is above the expected voltage window.

P25CD.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P25CD.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the intake camshaft phaser on bank 2 in its base position at engine off.

P25CE.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P25CE.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is below the expected voltage window.

P25CF.title: Intake Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 2
P25CF.description: The intake camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is above the expected voltage window.

P25D0.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 1
P25D0.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 1 in its base position at engine off.

P25D1.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P25D1.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is below the expected voltage window.

P25D2.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 1
P25D2.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 1 is above the expected voltage window.

P25D3.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit / Open Bank 2
P25D3.description: The controller cannot drive the park-lock pin that secures the exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 2 in its base position at engine off.

P25D4.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P25D4.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is below the expected voltage window.

P25D5.title: Exhaust Camshaft Actuator Park Lock Control Circuit High Bank 2
P25D5.description: The exhaust camshaft park-lock control line on bank 2 is above the expected voltage window.

P25D6.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Position Sensor Stop Performance
P25D6.description: During self-calibration of the exhaust heat exchanger bypass valve A, the position sensor never reached the expected mechanical stop.

P25D7.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit
P25D7.description: A third fuel level sensor (C) used on multi-tank trucks, dual-saddle SUVs, or auxiliary fuel systems returns no usable signal.

P25D8.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Performance
P25D8.description: The third fuel level sensor reading does not change as expected with consumption or refuelling.

P25D9.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit Low
P25D9.description: The third fuel level sensor signal is below the lower diagnostic threshold.

P25DA.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit High
P25DA.description: The third fuel level sensor signal is above the upper diagnostic threshold.

P25DB.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Circuit Intermittent
P25DB.description: The third fuel level sensor signal jumps or drops out for short moments.

P25DC.title: Fuel Level Sensor C Stuck
P25DC.description: The third fuel level sensor reads a constant value across known consumption or refuelling events.

P25DD.title: A Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 1
P25DD.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 will not unlock from its base position.

P25DE.title: A Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 1
P25DE.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages.

P25DF.title: A Camshaft Position Control Performance Bank 1
P25DF.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 1 follows the commanded angle too slowly, oscillates, or shows steady-state error outside tolerance.

P25E0.title: A Camshaft Position - Stuck In Locked Position Bank 2
P25E0.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 will not unlock from its base position.

P25E1.title: A Camshaft Position - Unable to Achieve Locked Position Bank 2
P25E1.description: Camshaft phaser A on bank 2 cannot reach its base position at engine shutdown so the lock pin never engages.

U3001.title: Control Module Improper Shutdown Performance
U3001.description: The control module did not complete its shutdown sequence cleanly — power was lost before housekeeping (saving learned values, freeze frames, adaptations) finished.

U3004.title: Accessory Power Relay

U3005.title: Retained Accessory Power
U3005.description: Fault on the retained accessory power (RAP) function that keeps comfort loads (windows, radio) powered for a short time after the key is removed.

U3006.title: Control Module Input Power A Circuit/Open

U3007.title: Control Module Input Power B Circuit/Open

U3009.title: Control Module Ground B
U3009.description: Control Module Ground B: the control module has detected this fault condition.

U300A.title: Ignition Switch
U300A.description: The control module detects an inconsistent or implausible ignition switch state — multiple positions reported simultaneously, or the position contradicts other inputs.

U300B.title: Ignition Input Accessory/On/Start
U300B.description: Fault on the combined ACC/ON/START ignition input line of the control module.

U300C.title: Ignition Input Off/On/Start
U300C.description: Fault on the OFF/ON/START ignition input line.

U300D.title: Ignition Input On/Start
U300D.description: Fault on the ON/START ignition input line — module sees inconsistent ON or START signal.

U300E.title: Ignition Input On
U300E.description: Fault on the ignition ON input — module does not see ON state when other inputs say ON, or vice versa.

U300F.title: Ignition Input Accessory
U300F.description: Fault on the ignition ACC (accessory) input.

U3010.title: Ignition Input Start
U3010.description: Fault on the ignition START input — module does not see start request when cranking, or sees one when not cranking.
